items.title: Duplicate of #7: generate typed mutations around changed optimization guards
items.body:
## Action
Add a bounded, change-directed mode to the existing pass comparison tools. Use a rewrite's regression seed and typed dependency neighborhood to exercise both successful and rejected guard conditions.

## Research basis
**Optimization-Directed Compiler Fuzzing for Continuous Translation Validation** (Optimuzz), Kwon et al., PLDI 2025, sections 3–4: https://prosys.kaist.ac.kr/publications/pldi25.pdf ; https://doi.org/10.1145/3729275 . The paper combines directed generation with translation validation. Its LLVM/TurboFan integrations are not drop-in Starshine implementations.

## Existing work and dependency
Build on #8, `src/validate/gen_valid.mbt`, `src/fuzz`, `scripts/lib/pass-fuzz-compare-task.ts`, and the existing generator profiles, semantic oracle, and reducer. Do not introduce another top-level harness or replace `HotFunc` as the owned IR.

## Possible implementation
1. Accept a selected rule ID, seed fixture, and explicit work budget. Resolve rule IDs through the diagnostic map rather than parsing arbitrary source code.
2. Start with CFG-preserving substitutions in a small def-use neighborhood: same-typed constants, signed/unsigned boundaries, operand aliasing, reused local sources, and alternate producers.
3. Add paired inputs on either side of a rewrite precondition. For effect-sensitive rules, place existing supported effectful producers before and after the candidate without violating typing.
4. Validate every candidate independently. Invalid generation, unsupported features, timeout, no firing, and semantic disagreement must remain different outcomes.
5. Retain candidates using new rule/guard coverage, not merely program size or broad line coverage. Preserve a portion of unguided inputs to avoid one-rule overfitting.
6. Use the existing reducer with a predicate that preserves the selected rule firing and the original mismatch class.

## Acceptance criteria
- Demonstrate a bounded improvement in selected-rule firing versus the current generator using identical seeds, input counts, and time limits.
- Include near-miss controls, unchanged-rule controls, and seeded faulty transformations that the oracle rejects.
- Replay metadata identifies source/binary hashes, rule map, feature policy, input seed, pass options, and observation mode.
- A timeout or unsupported semantic case never counts as verified equivalence.

## Constraints
This is test tooling, not a production optimization. Reuse bounded scratch and enforce mutation/depth/output limits. No always-on telemetry or solver dependency in release builds. Preserve `agent-todo.md` ownership of P00 and performance work; use small focused runs during development and leave long campaigns deferred. Do not create the separate private cross-project research harness.

items.title: DUPLICATE of #1995 — PRODUCT COMPLIANCE BLOCK
items.body:
CODEX_READY:true
TASK_MODE:REAL_DELIVERABLES
PRIORITY:P1_COMPLIANCE_DATA

## VERIFIED SOURCE / OWNER CHECK
- Current production source: `Catalog/Models.cs::CatalogProduct`, `Catalog/CatalogStore.cs` canonical product persistence, and channel-plan/readiness surfaces in `ChannelProductsStore.cs` / `ChannelProductsPanel.cs`.
- Current `CatalogProduct` model has product identity/content/pricing/stock/media fields but no structured producer/manufacturer or Türkiye importer block.
- Verified MarketplaceHub task source: task-pack T145 (`PRODUCT-COMPLIANCE`), sourced from Entegrasyon transcript #012, requires Türkiye-resident producer/importer information as typed product metadata with owner `Catalog/Models.cs; Catalog/CatalogStore.cs; ChannelProductsStore.cs/Panel.cs`.
- Open/closed issue search for producer/importer/product-compliance ownership returned no exact issue. Raw PR search for compliance/producer/importer returned zero PRs.
- No legal requirement, marketplace field name, endpoint or blocking rule is invented by this issue; it adds the data model needed to hold verified information.

## REAL PRODUCTION DELIVERABLE
1. Add a structured optional compliance-party block to the canonical product model for producer/manufacturer and Türkiye importer roles. Each party must have explicit role + legal/business name + business contact/address fields required by the application's verified compliance workflow, not a single unstructured notes string.
2. Support more than one importer only through an explicit bounded collection with stable item identity/order; do not silently collapse second/third importers into free text.
3. Define technical/domain bounds for every field, Unicode/control-character handling, null/missing semantics and canonical country/role representation. Missing data remains `UNKNOWN`, never fabricated from brand or seller name.
4. Add field/source provenance and observed/verified metadata so manual research, official catalog/packaging evidence or later verified import sources can be distinguished. Do not mark data verified merely because it exists.
5. Persist/save/reload through the canonical CatalogStore JSON contract; legacy products without the block remain readable as unknown and migration is idempotent.
6. Product workspace must allow explicit edit/clear with existing product stale/revision guard. A source/import update cannot silently overwrite newer manual verified data without the canonical ownership rule.
7. Provide a bounded product-detail/read projection usable by future compliance validation/readiness. Do not add marketplace live write in this task.
8. Sensitive contact/address fields must not be copied into generic diagnostics/audit text. Audit may record field group + source/reason, not raw address/email/phone.

## REAL PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT
Product workspace / verified catalog-import source -> `CatalogProduct` compliance parties -> `CatalogStore` save/reload -> product detail and later compliance readiness consumers.

## ACCEPTANCE / TESTS
- Product with one producer + primary importer round-trips across restart exactly, including roles/provenance.
- Product with explicitly supported second/third importer preserves stable order/identity and does not merge parties.
- Missing producer/importer remains unknown; brand/company names are never guessed into the block.
- Oversized/control-character/invalid role or country values fail with typed validation and zero catalog mutation.
- Legacy product JSON without compliance block reads normally and remains unchanged until explicitly edited.
- Two editors load same product; stale editor cannot overwrite a newer compliance edit.
- Import source without compliance fields does not erase manual values; explicitly mapped verified source follows ownership/provenance rules.
- Audit/support package fixtures contain no raw business email/phone/address from the block.
- 100k-product read/search remains bounded by existing catalog paging; adding the metadata must not force a new full-catalog materialization path.

## EDGE CASES
- manufacturer also acts as importer
- multiple importers with same display name but different identity
- sole-trader/contact fields that may contain personal data
- Turkish/Unicode legal names and addresses
- explicit clear versus source-missing
- corrupt legacy JSON/newer unknown fields
- import/manual edit race

## SECURITY / SAFETY
- Treat contact/address data as potentially sensitive/PII for logging/export purposes. Never put raw email/phone/address, credentials, token/PAT/password/API keys or secret-bearing URLs in diagnostics/issues/fixtures.
- Local catalog metadata only; no marketplace endpoint/scope/capability and no live write.
- Any future marketplace mutation of compliance fields must require immutable preview + explicit approval + stale/revision + idempotency + exact wrong-store/account guard.
- Do not add Paket/Set/Bundle, Varyant Sistemi, Hızlı Satır İçi Düzenleme, Kritik Fiyat, XML Varyant Mapping, Fulfillment Core or Hakediş/Mutabakat Core.

items.title: DUPLICATE of #111 — XML ITEMPATH CONTRACT
items.body:
CODEX_READY:true
TASK_MODE:REAL_DELIVERABLES
PRIORITY:P1_INPUT_INTEGRITY

## VERIFIED SOURCE / OWNER CHECK
- Current production source: `Catalog/XmlCatalog.cs` -> `Inspect`, `Preview`, `Document`, `PathOf`.
- `Inspect(xml,itemPath)` currently executes `d.XPathSelectElements(itemPath).ToList()` for a caller-supplied ItemPath. `Preview(xml,source)` executes `Document(xml).XPathSelectElements(source.ItemPath)` directly.
- The source validates mapped field-relative paths with a restrictive regex, but there is no equivalent canonical grammar/preflight for `ItemPath` itself before XPath evaluation.
- Auto-discovery already produces simple absolute element paths through `PathOf`, so the production contract can be constrained to the path shapes the application actually emits rather than accepting arbitrary XPath expressions.
- Open/closed issue search for XmlCatalog ItemPath/XPath validation returned no exact owner; raw PR search for `XmlCatalog ItemPath XPath` returned no PR.
- Existing XML owners for 25 MB document bounds, DTD prohibition, SSRF/fetching, source mapping and XML Variant Mapping are not reopened. XML Variant Mapping remains explicitly out of scope.

## VERIFIED PRODUCTION GAP
A malformed ItemPath can surface XPath parser/evaluation exceptions outside the application's typed validation path. More importantly, arbitrary XPath syntax (descendant selectors, unions, predicates/functions, etc.) can select a much broader or semantically different node set than the simple repeat-node path the XML import UI is designed around. `Inspect` also materializes every match before taking a 20-row sample, making broad/wrong ItemPath expressions unnecessarily expensive even though the source XML itself is bounded.

## REAL PRODUCTION DELIVERABLE
1. Define one canonical product-repeat ItemPath grammar shared by `Inspect` and `Preview`, derived from the existing `PathOf` output and current non-variant XML workflow. At minimum support deterministic absolute element-only paths required by auto-discovery; reject unsupported XPath operators/functions/predicates/unions/descendant tricks with a typed actionable validation error.
2. Compile/validate ItemPath before evaluation. No raw `XPathException`/`ArgumentException` may escape normal Inspect/Preview UI flows for user-configured paths.
3. Preserve current namespace-normalization behavior from `Document`; validation must happen against the normalized local-name document contract rather than inventing namespace mappings.
4. Make Inspect counting/sampling bounded in memory: return the true match count required by the current `XmlScan` contract, but do not materialize all matching `XElement` objects merely to keep the first 20/sample 3 rows. Iterate/count with bounded sample retention or an equivalent allocation-safe strategy.
5. Keep the existing 100,000-product Preview ceiling deterministic. ItemPath validation failure or too-many-items failure occurs before any catalog mutation.
6. Ensure source configuration save/test paths reuse the same canonical validator so a path accepted by Inspect cannot later fail under Preview because of grammar drift.

## REAL PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT
XML source workspace -> source test/inspect -> `XmlCatalog.Inspect` -> saved ItemPath -> `XmlCatalog.Preview` -> catalog import preview/apply.

## ACCEPTANCE / TESTS
- Auto-discovered `/root/products/product`-style path passes Inspect and Preview with identical node selection.
- Empty/whitespace, malformed bracket/quote syntax, union (`|`), arbitrary predicate/function, descendant (`//`) and unsupported axis expressions fail with typed validation messages; no raw XPath parser exception reaches UI.
- A valid path with zero matches reports the existing explicit no-record condition.
- 100,000 matching products remain supported under the existing Preview limit; 100,001 fails deterministically before catalog mutation.
- Inspect over a large bounded document reports the exact match count while retaining only bounded sample/path-discovery state, not a list of every match.
- Namespace-bearing source remains compatible with the current local-name normalization behavior.
- ItemPath accepted during source validation remains accepted after restart and by Preview.
- Malformed field-relative mapping paths continue to be rejected under their existing separate rules.

## EDGE CASES
- Unicode XML element names permitted by the application's actual normalized-name contract
- root-only path and deeply nested but bounded paths
- duplicate local names at different depths
- namespace prefixes removed during normalization
- zero matches, exactly 100k, 100001
- invalid XPath tokens that previously threw from `XPathSelectElements`
- source settings edited after Inspect but before Preview

## SECURITY / SAFETY
- Preserve `DtdProcessing.Prohibit`, `XmlResolver=null`, 25 MB document bound and all existing remote-fetch protections.
- No secret/token/PAT/password/API key/PII or raw supplier payload is logged in validation diagnostics.
- No marketplace endpoint/scope/capability and no remote marketplace write is introduced.
- Any downstream live marketplace mutation remains subject to immutable preview + explicit approval + stale/revision + idempotency + exact wrong-store guard.
- Do not add Paket/Set/Bundle, Varyant Sistemi, Hızlı Satır İçi Düzenleme, Kritik Fiyat, XML Varyant Mapping, Fulfillment Core or Hakediş/Mutabakat Core.

items.title: DUPLICATE of #2009 — SAFE LOCAL UNLINK
items.body:
CODEX_READY:true
TASK_MODE:REAL_DELIVERABLES
PRIORITY:P1_DATA_INTEGRITY

## VERIFIED SOURCE / OWNER CHECK
- Current production source: `ChannelProductsStore.cs` persists local `ChannelPlans`; `ChannelProductsPanel.cs` can load/edit/save a plan but exposes no unlink/remove workflow.
- Current store has `Find/List/CorruptPlans/Save/SaveBatch`; there is no revision-bound local unlink operation in the verified source.
- Verified task source: `MarketplaceHub-200-Iliskili-Production-Gorevi.md` T159 requires safe local unlink, explicitly stating that unlink is not remote delete/pause and must use dependency preview + confirmation.
- Open/closed issue search for ChannelProducts local unlink/dependency preview/confirmation returned no exact owner; matching PR search returned none.
- #2898 owns external-id uniqueness; #2899 owns link provenance. This issue owns operator unlink lifecycle only.

## REAL PRODUCTION DELIVERABLE
1. Add an explicit local unlink command for one canonical `(ChannelId,ShopId,ProductId)` plan. Unlink must never call a marketplace delete/pause/deactivate endpoint and must never claim the remote listing changed.
2. Before commit, build an immutable dependency preview showing exactly which local artifacts will lose/retain the link identity (listing matrix state, pending local sync references if any, provenance/evidence state, local notes/plan data policy).
3. Require explicit operator confirmation bound to plan Version/revision. If the plan changed after preview, return `STALE/REVIEW_REQUIRED` and perform zero mutation.
4. Choose and document one deterministic local state transition: either clear only link identity/evidence while retaining the local pricing/stock draft, or archive/delete the full plan only when no dependent local state would be lost. Do not silently discard unrelated notes/pricing/stock draft data.
5. If dependent pending/running local sync work refers to the link, unlink must fail closed or cancel through its existing owner with a typed review result; do not orphan a job or retarget it.
6. Concurrency: two unlink attempts or unlink racing Save/relink must have one deterministic winner under CAS; stale caller cannot delete/clear a newer plan.
7. UI must clearly say “yerel bağlantıyı kaldır” and after success show remote state as unknown/unchanged rather than “silindi”.

## REAL PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT
`ChannelProductsPanel` selected product/shop -> Unlink preview -> explicit confirmation -> `ChannelProductsStore` revision-bound local mutation -> Listing Matrix/local plan refresh.

## ACCEPTANCE / TESTS
- Linked local plan -> preview -> confirm -> local link identity is removed according to documented policy; no network request occurs.
- Cancel at confirmation -> byte-for-byte no DB mutation.
- Save/relink after preview bumps Version -> stale unlink fails with zero mutation.
- Two processes confirm same preview -> one success, one stale/not-found result; no partial state.
- Pending/running local sync dependency is detected and handled fail-closed according to existing Sync owner; no orphan reference.
- Unlink does not delete product, remote listing, credentials, audit history or unrelated shop data.
- Retained local draft fields remain exactly preserved if clear-link policy is chosen.
- #2899 evidence is cleared/invalidated atomically with link identity; no verified evidence survives an unlinked plan.
- #2898 uniqueness slot becomes reusable only after successful committed unlink and not before.
- Restart after success keeps unlinked state; crash before commit leaves old state intact.

## EDGE CASES
- already-unlinked plan
- corrupt plan row
- stale Version
- duplicate legacy external-id collision under #2898 review
- unlink racing SaveBatch/relink
- DB busy/locked
- selected product deleted/deactivated locally while preview is open
- channel/shop connection disabled between preview and commit

## SECURITY / SAFETY
- Local-only operation; network/marketplace write count must be zero.
- No secret/token/PAT/password/API key/PII/raw ListingUrl in preview diagnostics/logs.
- Parameterized SQL and revision/CAS; no force-delete fallback.
- A future remote delete/pause feature would be a separate task and must use preview + explicit approval + stale/revision + idempotency + exact wrong-store protection.
- Do not add Paket/Set/Bundle, Varyant Sistemi, Hızlı Satır İçi Düzenleme, Kritik Fiyat, XML Varyant Mapping, Fulfillment Core or Hakediş/Mutabakat Core.

CODEX_READY:true
TASK_MODE:REAL_DELIVERABLES
PRIORITY:P1_TRACEABILITY

- Current production source: `ChannelProductsStore.cs` and `ChannelProductsPanel.cs`.
- Current persisted `ChannelProductPlan` snapshot written by `SaveWithinTransaction` contains ChannelId, ShopId, ProductId, ListingId, ListingUrl, TargetCategory, PlannedPrice, Currency, PlannedStock, Notes, UpdatedUtc and Version; it does not persist how the ListingId/ListingUrl was obtained or when/if it was verified.
- The current WPF editor labels ListingId/ListingUrl as manually entered and unverified, but that state is presentation text rather than durable data; after save/restart there is no typed provenance separating manual input from a future verified read-only connector result.
- Verified task source: `MarketplaceHub-200-Iliskili-Production-Gorevi.md` T158 requires URL/manual/API-read source + `verifiedAt` metadata while forbidding raw URL logging.
- Open/closed issue search for ChannelProducts link provenance/evidence/verifiedAt returned no exact owner; matching PR search returned none.
- #2898 owns external-id uniqueness; this issue owns evidence/provenance only and must consume that identity invariant rather than reimplement it.

## REAL PRODUCTION DELIVERABLE
1. Extend the local channel-link model with a typed provenance state for the existing link fields, at minimum distinguishing `MANUAL_UNVERIFIED` from `VERIFIED_READ` and `UNKNOWN_LEGACY`. Do not invent remote verification where no verified connector read exists.
2. Never persist access tokens, authorization headers, raw response bodies or a URL containing credentials/query secrets.
3. Existing manually entered ListingId/ListingUrl saves must become explicit `MANUAL_UNVERIFIED`; the UI must render that truth after restart instead of implying verification.
4. A verified-read provenance may only be set by a concrete connector path that can prove the exact channel/shop/account and external listing identity. UI/manual callers cannot forge `VERIFIED_READ` merely by setting a flag.
5. Evidence becomes stale/review-required when the local link identity changes, the bound shop changes, or a new plan revision replaces the evidence-bearing identity. Do not carry old verification onto a different ListingId.
6. Migrate existing rows deterministically to `UNKNOWN_LEGACY`/manual-unverified without making a trust claim. No remote calls during migration.
7. List/Find/corruption diagnostics must validate the provenance domain and timestamp storage safely; malformed evidence isolates the row for review rather than silently upgrading trust.

## REAL PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT
`ChannelProductsPanel` manual plan editor and any verified read-only connector link flow -> `ChannelProductsStore.Save/SaveBatch` -> `channel_products.db/ChannelPlans` -> listing matrix/operator review surfaces.

## ACCEPTANCE / TESTS
- Manual ListingId/URL save reads back after restart as `MANUAL_UNVERIFIED`, with no VerifiedAt timestamp.
- A verified-read test adapter bound to exact channel/shop/listing can persist `VERIFIED_READ` + canonical UTC VerifiedAt; changing ListingId invalidates prior evidence.
- Manual caller attempting to persist `VERIFIED_READ` without connector evidence is rejected.
- Legacy pre-migration rows become deterministic `UNKNOWN_LEGACY`/unverified state; no guessed verification date.
- Raw URL containing query token/userinfo is never written to audit/evidence diagnostics; redacted/bounded metadata only.
- Malformed future/invalid timestamp and unknown evidence enum are surfaced as REVIEW_REQUIRED, not treated as verified.
- Save/SaveBatch Version/CAS semantics remain intact and a failed provenance validation causes zero mutation.
- #2898 duplicate external-id conflict still wins before any conflicting row is presented as verified.
- Restart and multi-instance read/write preserve evidence exactly once without stale evidence resurrection.

## EDGE CASES
- blank ListingId with stale old evidence
- ListingUrl changes while ListingId stays same
- exact same external id reverified later
- shop/channel change
- clock skew/future VerifiedAt
- legacy row with no new fields
- corrupt evidence storage class or oversized evidence reference

## SECURITY / SAFETY
- Local metadata/read-evidence only; no marketplace mutation and no new endpoint/scope/capability claim.
- No secret/token/PAT/password/API key/authorization header/PII/raw provider response/raw secret-bearing URL in DB diagnostics, logs or fixtures.
- Verified provenance must include exact wrong-store/account evidence; absence means unverified, never best-effort success.

items.title: Duplicate of #7: measure rewrite-rule coverage in pass-local comparisons
items.body:
## Action
Extend the existing pass-local comparison lane with coverage of individual rewrite decisions. A successful run must distinguish a pass that was invoked from a rewrite that actually changed the input.

This is a proposed testing improvement, not a report of a confirmed compiler defect.

## Research basis
Kwon et al., **Optimization-Directed Compiler Fuzzing for Continuous Translation Validation**, PLDI 2025, sections 3–4. The transferable idea is to aim testing at specific optimization conditions instead of relying on whole-compiler coverage.
- Paper: https://prosys.kaist.ac.kr/publications/pldi25.pdf
- DOI: https://doi.org/10.1145/3729275

## Existing implementation and scope
Reuse `src/passes`, `src/cmd/optimizer_reports.mbt`, `scripts/lib/pass-fuzz-compare-task.ts`, and `scripts/lib/fuzz-summary-counters.ts`. `docs/wiki/tooling/pass-fuzz-compare.md` already describes pass admission, minimum comparison counts, semantic execution, and reduction. Do not rebuild those features. Check existing counters first and add only missing rule-level information.

## Possible implementation
1. Give a small initial set of OptimizeInstructions and DAE2 rewrite sites stable diagnostic IDs. Keep the ID mapping separate from source line numbers.
2. Record bounded counts for candidate visited, guard rejected, rewrite committed, and later invalidated/rolled back where applicable. Count a rewrite only after the mutation succeeds.
3. Include pass options, input hash, source revision, rule-map version, and actual firing counts in existing comparison artifacts.
4. Add an opt-in requirement that selected rules fire at least a configured number of times. Reject unknown rule IDs. A zero-fire lane must be reported as insufficient coverage, not successful qualification.
5. Keep aggregate reporting separate from semantic results. Rule firing does not establish correctness or profitability.

## Tests and acceptance criteria
- A small fixture fires each initial rule; a near-miss fixture reaches the guard but does not fire it.
- A disabled rule and a no-op pass fail the required-fire gate.
- Output bytes and observable behavior agree with ordinary builds when diagnostics are disabled.
- Compare original and transformed programs through the existing semantic lane; retain trap and effect-order observations.
- Report coverage of the selected rule set, not all Starshine optimizations.

## Cost and integration constraints
Diagnostics must be opt-in. Avoid persistent per-node strings, new ordinary-path allocations, and unbounded event logs. Use compact counters and reusable storage. items.title: Windows: Minimize and Close ignore Moonlight touch input (duplicate of #47289)

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
Correction after retesting: **Maximize/Restore works in Moonlight touch mode. Only Minimize and Close fail.** Closing as a duplicate of #47289 at the reporter’s request.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.930.31730 (build 12947, prod), confirmed through the desktop app's version/update-check tool.
Microsoft Store package version: OpenAI.Codex 26.930.3930.0.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided. This report concerns desktop window input behavior.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows, Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.22631.0, x64.
Accessing the Windows desktop through Moonlight streaming with touch mode enabled.
Moonlight client platform/version and streaming host software/version have not been collected.

### What issue are you seeing?

In the Codex Windows desktop app, Moonlight touch mode cannot activate the top-right Minimize and Close (X) controls. Maximize / Restore works in touch mode after retesting.

This is localized to those three buttons among the controls tested. Touch input works on the top-left File, Edit, View, and Help menus, the back-navigation control, split-pane controls, and the chat/content area. The app remains responsive. Other controls have not been exhaustively tested.

Switching the same streaming session to Moonlight mouse mode makes all three top-right buttons work normally.

| Control | Moonlight touch mode | Moonlight mouse mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimize | No window action | Works |
| Maximize / Restore | Works | Works |
| Close | No window action | Works |

These input results were confirmed by the user during troubleshooting; they were not reproduced through automated touch injection.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Stream a Windows desktop running Codex through Moonlight.
2. Enable Moonlight touch mode.
3. Open Codex and tap each of the three top-right window controls.
4. Observe that Minimize and Close do not perform their window actions, while Maximize/Restore works.
5. Tap the top-left menus, back-navigation control, or split-pane controls and observe that touch interaction works.
6. Switch Moonlight to mouse mode.
7. Click the same three top-right window controls and observe that all work normally.

### What is the expected behavior?

Touch-mode input delivered through Moonlight should activate the three window controls, just as mouse-mode input does, while retaining normal touch interaction elsewhere in the app.

### Additional information

Duplicate of #47289. After retesting, the reporter confirmed the same affected controls: Minimize and Close fail with touch, while Maximize/Restore works. This observation was made through Moonlight streaming.

Read-only inspection of the installed app bundle found Windows window configuration using `titleBarStyle: "hidden"` and `titleBarOverlay`. This is a diagnostic clue, not proof of a root cause. It is not yet established whether the failure originates in Codex/Electron's window controls, the streaming input translation, or their interaction.

Current workaround: use Moonlight mouse mode for these three controls. No application files or system input settings were changed during investigation.

items.body:
CODEX_READY:true
TASK_MODE:REAL_DELIVERABLES
PRIORITY:P1_ORDER_IDENTITY

## VERIFIED SOURCE / OWNER CHECK
- Current production source: `OrdersModels.cs::OrderItem` contains only `Title`, `Sku`, `Quantity`; there is no persisted local-product match state/id/evidence on an order line.
- `OrdersStore.cs` persists the whole `OrderSnapshot` JSON and merges remote order refreshes, but it has no catalog-line resolution state or durable unmatched marker.
- Verified task source: `MarketplaceHub-200-Iliskili-Production-Gorevi.md` T193 requires: “Catalog eşleşmezse fake product oluşturmadan UNMATCHED state sakla.” Entry owner is `OrdersStore.cs/order-line projection; Catalog/CatalogStore.cs identity lookup; settings workspace`.
- Open/closed issue search for unmatched order line / undefined product / fake product / manual match returned no matching issue. PR search returned only PR #11 (Etsy listing detail + stock decision); its inspected diff owns Etsy stock decision/listing detail and does not implement durable unmatched order-line state.

## REAL PRODUCTION DELIVERABLE
1. Give each durable order line a stable local line identity within `(Marketplace,ShopId,OrderId)` that survives restart and remote replay even when title text changes. Do not use list index as the durable identity if the provider supplies/verifies a stronger line identity; when it does not, use a documented deterministic local identity with collision handling.
2. Add a typed persisted match state such as `UNMATCHED`, `MATCHED`, `REVIEW_REQUIRED` plus optional canonical local `ProductId`, product revision/evidence and match-source metadata. Legacy rows become unknown/unmatched deterministically; never guess a product.
3. Resolve local catalog identity only through existing canonical CatalogStore identity rules/lookup. If no single safe product exists, persist `UNMATCHED` or `REVIEW_REQUIRED`; **never create a CatalogProduct** just to make the order line look matched.
4. Preserve original remote `Title`/`Sku` evidence separately from any later local display fallback. Remote refresh may update remote evidence but must not silently overwrite a valid operator match; if evidence now contradicts the stored match, transition to REVIEW_REQUIRED instead of auto-retargeting.
5. An unmatched/review-required line is ineligible for automatic/local stock application. Existing order-stock owner must receive an explicit typed reason rather than a missing-SKU/null failure.
6. A previously matched product that is deleted, identity-collides, or becomes unreadable/corrupt causes review-required on the next validation; do not silently pick another product.
7. Persist/merge the state transactionally with order refresh so a crash cannot save new remote evidence while losing match state, or vice versa.
8. Provide bounded order-detail projection for match state/reason without customer PII or raw provider payload.

## REAL PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT
Connector order ingest/read -> `OrderNormalizer` / order-line projection -> canonical `CatalogStore` identity lookup -> `OrdersStore.SaveBatch` merge -> Orders UI / stock-decision consumer.

## ACCEPTANCE / TESTS
- Known unique SKU/catalog identity persists `MATCHED + ProductId`; restart/replay retains the same match.
- Unknown SKU persists `UNMATCHED`; zero CatalogProduct rows are created as a side effect.
- Two catalog candidates for the same canonical identity produce `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, never first-row-wins.
- Remote replay with same line identity but changed title updates remote evidence while preserving a still-valid manual/system match.
- Remote replay whose identity evidence now contradicts the matched product moves to REVIEW_REQUIRED and blocks stock apply.
- Legacy order payload with old `{Title,Sku,Quantity}` items migrates/readbacks safely without fabricated ProductId.
- OrderStock preview/apply receives an explicit unmatched/review-required failure and performs zero stock mutation.
- Corrupt/deleted matched product after restart is not silently replaced with another product.
- SaveBatch rollback leaves both order evidence and match state at the previous committed revision.
- Multi-instance refresh of the same order cannot erase a newer manual match through last-writer-wins.

## EDGE CASES
- blank SKU but unique verified barcode/external evidence if available
- repeated same SKU twice in one order as distinct lines
- title changes while SKU stays stable
- duplicate canonical SKU collision
- product deleted/deactivated/corrupt after match
- remote line removed/re-added on replay
- legacy order with no stable provider line id
- DB busy/locked/restart during merge

## SECURITY / SAFETY
- Local order/catalog metadata only; no marketplace write and no new endpoint/scope/capability.
- Never log raw order payload, customer name/address/phone/email, credentials, tokens, PATs, passwords or API keys. Diagnostics use bounded marketplace/shop/order/line identity + reason code only.
- Matching is fail-closed; no auto-create/auto-retarget fallback.
- Any later live marketplace write remains gated by immutable preview + explicit approval + stale/revision + idempotency + exact wrong-store/account guard.
- Paket/Set/Bundle, Varyant Sistemi, Hızlı Satır İçi Düzenleme, Kritik Fiyat, XML Varyant Mapping, Fulfillment Core and Hakediş/Mutabakat Core remain out of scope.

- Current production source: `Catalog/Models.cs`, `Catalog/CatalogStore.cs`, `ChannelProductsStore.cs` / `ChannelProductsPanel.cs` readiness surface.
- Current source has no dedicated product-compliance validator/policy owner for producer/importer/origin metadata.

3. Evaluation returns typed states such as `COMPLETE`, `WARNING`, `BLOCKED`, `POLICY_UNVERIFIED`, `POLICY_NOT_APPLICABLE` with bounded field/reason codes; never infer rules from channel name alone.
4. Scope resolution must be explicit and deterministic (for example local category/channel/shop only when the verified policy actually declares that scope). Unsupported/unknown scope fails closed to review, not to a fabricated requirement.
5. Policy edits use revision/CAS; a readiness preview produced under policy revision N becomes stale when policy or product compliance data changes before an apply/publish decision.
6. Existing products remain readable when no verified policy exists. Absence of policy must not silently block all products nor mark them compliant; surface `POLICY_UNVERIFIED/NOT_CONFIGURED` truthfully.
7. Validation is pure/local and causes zero marketplace writes. Downstream publish/readiness consumers may block on its typed result but cannot bypass existing live-write gates.
8. Diagnostics/audit store only policy id/revision + bounded missing-field codes; never raw company contact/address/evidence payloads.

- Verified active policy requiring producer legal name: missing field returns BLOCKED; present valid field returns COMPLETE.
- Same rule marked warning-only returns WARNING, not BLOCKED.
- Unverified/advisory policy cannot block even if its condition fails.
- Policy revision changes after readiness preview -> stale result rejected and new evaluation required.
- Product compliance data revision changes after preview -> stale result rejected.
- Category/channel/shop scope mismatch -> NOT_APPLICABLE; wrong-store policy cannot evaluate another shop as matching.

- unknown field code from newer policy version
- legacy/corrupt policy row
- product missing #2904/#2905 metadata blocks entirely
- channel/shop removed or disabled
- clock/effective-date boundaries if used by verified policy

A source update must not silently overwrite a manually owned/locked value if the existing ownership rules say not to.
4. Persist/save/reload/search-detail projection through the canonical CatalogStore product path; restart must preserve exact decimal values and units deterministically.

- zero entered intentionally versus missing
- very small positive decimals and maximum accepted boundary
- unit conversion display without changing canonical stored value
- import/manual ownership race

- old JSON payload with unknown/newer fields

- Verified task source: task-pack T155 requires wrong-store link preflight and T156 requires product/channel/shop/external-id preview bound to revision.
- Open/closed issue search for ChannelProducts wrong-store link preflight/stale binding returned no exact owner. Raw GitHub PR search for ChannelProducts + wrong-store + link preview returned zero PRs.
- #2898 owns external-id uniqueness, #2899 evidence metadata, #2900 unlink. This issue owns creation/relink scope preflight + approval binding only.

## REAL PRODUCTION DELIVERABLE
1. Replace free-text-only link commit semantics with a typed scope object bound to canonical `ChannelId`, a concrete local connection/shop identity when one exists, `ProductId`, current plan Version, proposed external ListingId and provenance state.
2. Build an immutable link/relink preview before changing a non-empty ListingId. Show old/new listing identity, exact channel/shop, local product identity and whether shop evidence is verified or manual/unverified.
3. A verified external link may not be committed as verified unless the evidence proves the exact selected channel/shop/account. Manual/unverified links may remain supported as explicit local drafts, but the UI/state must say `UNVERIFIED` and never upgrade them to verified implicitly.
4. Commit must compare the preview-bound Version/scope with current state. Product selection, shop, connection revision, plan Version or proposed ListingId changing after preview invalidates approval and requires a fresh preview.
5. Do not silently retarget a plan when `shop.Text` changes. Current `loadedShop != shop.Text.Trim()` guard remains and is strengthened with canonical connection identity/revision where available.
6. Integrate #2898 conflict check and #2899 provenance: wrong-store/stale/conflict/evidence failures all produce zero mutation and preserve the editor buffer.
7. This is local link metadata only. Do not add a remote listing mutation or infer provider ownership from URL shape alone.

## REAL PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT
`ChannelProductsPanel` product + shop selection -> ListingId/URL edit -> link preview -> explicit confirm -> `ChannelProductsStore` CAS commit -> listing matrix refresh.

## ACCEPTANCE / TESTS
- Existing plan at Version N: change ListingId -> preview -> confirm -> exactly one N→N+1 commit.
- Change shop/product/ListingId or reload a newer plan after preview -> approval becomes stale; zero mutation.
- Verified-read evidence for shop A cannot be committed under shop B.
- Manual/unverified link can be saved only with explicit unverified state and is visibly unverified after restart.
- Disabled/missing connection does not get silently substituted with another `default` shop; verified path fails closed/review-required.
- Two windows preview same Version; first commits relink, second fails stale.
- #2898 duplicate external id conflict produces typed conflict, no partial provenance/plan write.
- Cancel preview/confirmation leaves DB unchanged.
- DB busy/locked and corrupt target remain distinct from stale/wrong-store.
- No remote HTTP request is issued by preview or local commit.

## EDGE CASES
- free-text legacy shop with no connection row
- `default` shop name collision
- channel casing/whitespace
- connection disabled/reconfigured between preview and commit
- listing identity cleared vs replaced
- legacy plan with unknown provenance
- duplicate listing collision discovered during commit

## SECURITY / SAFETY
- No secret/token/PAT/password/API key/PII/raw secret-bearing URL in preview, logs or diagnostics.
- Wrong-store/account evidence is mandatory for any verified state; lack of evidence is UNVERIFIED, not success.
- Parameterized SQL and revision/CAS; no force-overwrite.
- If any future live marketplace write is ever added downstream, immutable preview + explicit approval + stale/revision + idempotency + exact wrong-store/account guard are mandatory before dispatch.
- No new endpoint/scope/provider capability is invented.
- Paket/Set/Bundle, Varyant Sistemi, Hızlı Satır İçi Düzenleme, Kritik Fiyat, XML Varyant Mapping, Fulfillment Core and Hakediş/Mutabakat Core remain out of scope.

items.title: DUPLICATE of #2007 — CHANNEL PLAN EXTERNAL-ID UNIQUENESS
items.body:
CODEX_READY:true
TASK_MODE:REAL_DELIVERABLES
PRIORITY:P0_DATA_INTEGRITY

## VERIFIED SOURCE / OWNER CHECK
- Current production source: `ChannelProductsStore.cs` (`ChannelPlans` table, `ValidatePlan`, `Save`, `SaveBatch`, `SaveWithinTransaction`) and `ChannelProductsPanel.cs` local channel-plan editor.
- Current primary key is `(ChannelId,ShopId,ProductId)`. `ListingId` lives only inside the JSON payload; `SaveWithinTransaction` writes it without any `(ChannelId,ShopId,ListingId)` collision check/index.
- Therefore two different `ProductId` rows under the same channel/shop can persist the same non-empty external `ListingId` and both look healthy.
- Verified task source: `MarketplaceHub-200-Iliskili-Production-Gorevi.md` T157 requires: “Aynı channel/shop external listing iki local producta sessiz bağlanmasın.”
- Open/closed issue search for ChannelPlans/ListingId duplicate external-listing ownership returned no exact owner; PR search returned no matching PR.
- Related but not duplicate: #2871 owns ProductId canonical identity; #2863 owns bulk target identity. This issue owns external listing identity uniqueness only.

## REAL PRODUCTION DELIVERABLE
1. Add one canonical optional external-listing identity contract for `ChannelPlans`: a blank `ListingId` means unlinked/local draft; a non-blank id is unique within the exact canonical `(ChannelId,ShopId)` scope.
2. Enforce the invariant transactionally for both `Save` and `SaveBatch`; do not rely on UI pre-checks. Two processes racing to link the same external id must produce one winner and one typed conflict/review result.
3. Preserve current `(ChannelId,ShopId,ProductId)` primary identity and Version/CAS behavior. A failed external-id conflict must mutate neither row and must not increment either version.
4. Legacy DB migration must detect existing collisions before installing any supporting unique structure. Never auto-pick a winner or delete/rewrite a plan. Surface bounded `REVIEW_REQUIRED` collision diagnostics with channel/shop + involved local product ids only.
5. Normalize only according to a documented application-level external-id identity rule that is safe without inventing provider semantics. Do not case-fold/trim provider ids unless an existing verified connector contract proves it; at minimum reject control characters and apply technical length bounds already used for `ListingId`.
6. UI save failure must keep the editor buffer intact and explain that the external listing is already linked to another local product. It must not silently clear ListingId or overwrite the other plan.

## REAL PRODUCTION ENTRY POINT
`ChannelProductsPanel` -> local plan load/edit -> `ChannelProductsStore.Save/SaveBatch` -> `channel_products.db/ChannelPlans` -> listing matrix/sync-read projections.

## ACCEPTANCE / TESTS
- Save product A with channel `etsy`, shop S, ListingId L succeeds. Saving product B in the same channel/shop with L fails typed `EXTERNAL_ID_CONFLICT/REVIEW_REQUIRED`; A remains unchanged and B is not partially written.
- Same L in a different shop or different channel remains allowed.
- Blank ListingId can exist on many local draft rows.
- Two independent store instances race to assign the same L to different products: exactly one commit succeeds.
- SaveBatch containing an internal duplicate L rolls back the whole batch.
- SaveBatch racing an existing row collision rolls back the whole batch.
- Legacy DB with two conflicting rows is detected deterministically on restart/migration; neither row is auto-deleted/rewritten.
- Existing stale-Version CAS still rejects stale saves even when external id is unique.
- DB busy/locked is not mislabeled as an identity collision.
- Listing Matrix and ChannelProductsPanel never present both collided legacy rows as a normal healthy linked state without a review signal.

## EDGE CASES
- same ListingId with leading/trailing spaces
- non-ASCII ids and provider-specific case sensitivity
- id at exact technical max and max+1
- conflict row is corrupt/quarantined
- unlink/clear racing relink
- concurrent Save and SaveBatch
- restart after migration interruption

## SECURITY / SAFETY
- Local metadata only; no marketplace write and no new endpoint/scope/capability.
- Never log raw ListingUrl, credentials, tokens, PATs, passwords, API keys or PII. Conflict diagnostics are bounded identity metadata only.
- Parameterized SQL; no force-overwrite/auto-merge fallback.
- Any future live marketplace mutation consuming this link still requires immutable preview + explicit approval + stale/revision + idempotency + exact wrong-store/account guard.
- Do not add Paket/Set/Bundle, Varyant Sistemi, Hızlı Satır İçi Düzenleme, Kritik Fiyat, XML Varyant Mapping, Fulfillment Core or Hakediş/Mutabakat Core.

items.body:
### Description

Hi,

We started seeing this after last week's update. With CSS Print Method set to Internal Embedding, saving an Elementor page returns the page's CSS in front of the JSON response.

The save itself works. Changes are stored and a new revision is created. But the admin-ajax.php response for save_builder starts like this:

<style id="elementor-post-11277">
    .elementor-11277 .elementor-element.elementor-element-70a75d8e { ...
</style>
{"success":true,"data":{"responses":{"save_builder":{"success":true,"code":200, ...

Because the response isn't valid JSON, two things go wrong:

- In the Elementor editor, the Publish/Update button stays active after saving, and leaving the page brings up an unsaved changes warning. The console shows errors from web-cli.min.js and an "Uncaught (in promise)".
- In the block editor, saving an Elementor-built page gives "Updating failed. The response is not a valid JSON response." The REST response has the same <style> block at the start. Meta box data (Yoast SEO in our case) never saves, because it only goes through after a successful post save.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Elementor > Settings > Performance > CSS Print Method: Internal Embedding
2. Open a page in Elementor, change something, click Update
3. Look at the elementor_ajax response in DevTools > Network

We need Internal Embedding because our host's page cache was serving pages that linked to Elementor CSS files after they'd been regenerated, which left pages unstyled. For now we've worked around the bug by stripping the leading <style> block from save responses with a small output buffer. That fixes both editors, but we'd rather not keep it long term.

items.title: Duplicate of #109: anonymous organization base-table hardening
items.body:
Follow-up discovered during Issue #108 security-advisor classification.

## Finding
Anonymous RLS on active `organizations` / `organization_locations` plus default table grants allows direct anonymous SELECT of all base-table columns, including internal metadata such as `created_by`. Public discovery already has curated SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (`public_partner_directory`, `public_partner_profile`, `public_partner_profile_details`, `public_active_offers`) and current frontend code does not rely on anonymous direct table reads.

## Goal
Make the curated public RPCs the anonymous public-read boundary while preserving authenticated organization/editor behavior.

## Scope
- revoke anonymous SELECT on `public.organizations` and `public.organization_locations`;
- do not revoke authenticated reads;
- preserve anonymous EXECUTE on the four intentional public RPCs;
- add pgTAP/security regression proving anon cannot direct-select the two base tables but can still call the curated public RPCs;
- no schema/data deletion, no RLS weakening, no production DNS/provider changes.

## Acceptance
1. `anon` cannot SELECT base organization/location tables.
2. `authenticated` remains able to use existing organization/profile/editor flows under RLS.
3. Four curated public RPCs remain executable by anon and return only their declared public projection.
4. Database QA and normal repo gates are green.
5. Issue #108 records this as remediated rather than merely classified.

items.title: [Duplicate of #67] Define ongoing project reporting and decision handoff with external workspaces
items.body:
## 한국어 요약

개발이 시작된 뒤에도 사용자가 외부 프로젝트 공간에서 현황·문제·선택·승인을 관리하고, 그 결정이 GitHub 실행 원본에 정확히 반영되는 최소 규칙을 정의합니다. 완료된 #63의 작업 전 맥락 처리를 반복하지 않고, 작업 진행 중의 보고·판단·반영 확인을 다룹니다.

이번에는 후속 Discovery의 범위와 검증 시나리오를 등록합니다. Notion 전용 DB·자동화나 양방향 동기화 구현을 승인하지 않습니다. v0.1.0 마일스톤·출시 게이트·#62 보류·#65 대상 지정은 변경하지 않습니다. 현행 언어 정책에 따라 이 짧은 한국어 요약을 유지하며, 상세 언어 분담은 아래 조사 대상입니다.

## Classification and question

Bounded Discovery; follow-up to #63. Not assigned to a release milestone.

What minimal, optional contract lets a maintainer operate a project through an external workspace throughout delivery, while GitHub remains authoritative for repository execution contracts, tracked-Issue lifecycle, changes, review and verification?

An external workspace may own project-level context, priorities, coordination, decisions, and non-repository work. It is not limited to pre-project planning or a collection of links. This must not create a second independently edited lifecycle ledger for the same tracked Issue.

## Existing behavior and the gap to resolve

Read the current `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW_SPEC.md`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` before further work. The repository already defines pre-Issue context, concise decision promotion, authorization envelopes, independent Review/QA, durable continuation, and separate execution/merge/release authority. Reuse those rules rather than redefining them.

Clarify their ongoing cross-surface behavior: when to report meaningful progress, what a decision request must communicate, how an authorized external decision is reflected and verified in the execution record, and how stale, conflicting, or inaccessible information is handled.

## Scope and evidence needed

1. **Ongoing project reporting.** Define material triggers such as accepted results, blockers, scope changes, review outcomes and handoff. Identify the responsible updater, source references, observed-at point and unresolved facts. Avoid reports for every commit, raw transcript, or mandatory daily entry. Distinguish aggregate project phase/health from individual Issue Status.
2. **Decision request and authority.** State the exact choice, alternatives, recommendation and reason, consequences, material constraints, affected Issue/PR/contract revision and unresolved evidence. Preserve the authorized person's decision, scope and exclusions; a received choice, verified reflection into GitHub, execution, integration and release are distinct events.
3. **Reflection and recovery.** Define readback, duplicate/retry handling, stale-read checks, rejected/revised decisions, conflicting translations and unavailable integrations. Never infer approval from a label, comment resolution, notification, summary, or Issue creation. Pause only affected execution when required authority or evidence is unresolved; unrelated authorized work need not stop merely because optional reporting is unavailable.
4. **Language ownership.** Reconcile the desired English detailed GitHub records / Korean maintainer-facing workspace explanation with the current Korean-summary requirements in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and templates. Propose an explicit compatible policy or reviewed change; do not silently remove the current requirements or treat a translation as new authority.
5. **Record reuse.** Preserve sufficient links between applicable requirements, decisions, changes, current-revision verification and delivery for later document preparation. Consider point-in-time references and necessary evidence retention without adding a metadata system, transcripts, or seven mandatory documents to every Issue.
6. **Placement and optionality.** Recommend what belongs in the generic workflow contract, optional adapter guidance, or a separate workspace/publishing workflow. Notion is an example, not a runtime dependency. Keep repository operation possible without an external workspace.

## Scenarios for the proposed contract

- A maintainer reopens a project and can identify current progress, consequential blockers, next work and the source observation point without replaying a session.
- A decision authorizes implementation and PR preparation but explicitly forbids merge; the restriction survives the handoff.
- The external decision is recorded, but its GitHub update fails or has an ambiguous response; affected execution does not continue on assumed success, and retry first checks actual state.
- Source state changes or the two language versions disagree after a summary was written; the discrepancy is surfaced before dependent execution.
- A person intervenes or an agent session ends; the next executor uses current GitHub records and preserved changes, not a stale summary or missing local-only work.
- After delivery, a reader can identify the approved scope, selected alternative, actual change, verification target and known limits at the stated version; missing evidence is reported, not invented.
- Without Notion or another external workspace, the existing GitHub-only workflow remains usable. Proposed policy behavior is not claimed as an implemented integration.

## Decision and completion conditions

Record **Adopt, Split, Defer, or Reject** with rationale and placement.

Completion requires a concise gap analysis against existing rules; a responsibility/source matrix; a minimum reporting and decision-reflection model covering the scenarios above; explicit handling of language conflicts and update failures; a privacy and retention boundary; and a scoped recommendation for any further implementation or contract edits. Link existing provisions that already suffice. Do not create follow-up Issues for every writing step.

Distinguish a reviewed design/tabletop result from a live integration test or real-project dogfood. Any adopted normative repository change follows the normal Issue/PR/Review and authority path before it becomes effective.

## Constraints, authority and release scope

- The current request authorizes planning, initial scoping and registration of this work. It does not grant blanket authority to implement integrations, change canonical repository contracts, merge PRs, alter permissions, or publish a release.
- Re-scan the queue and confirm execution authority, required Dedicated User Project membership and actual lifecycle Status before starting the follow-up. Intended intake is Backlog, not automatic Ready or In Progress; registration is not proof of Project membership.
- Do not add this Issue to `v0.1.0`, alter frozen baseline estimates, make it a dependency of #65, resume #62, select a dogfood target, reopen #63, or request #39 release approval as a side effect.
- Keep #65 and the #38/#39 release gates unchanged. Whether any outcome belongs in the current release is a separate maintainer decision, not implied by this Issue.
- No new Notion databases, task mirrors, Jira adoption, global agent deployment, telemetry store, document-generation engine, account upgrade, or public/private support expansion is included.
- Do not copy private workspace URLs, personal/company/client data, credentials or full conversations into this public Issue. Approved public summaries must be sufficient for review without requiring access to private source material.

## Related records

- #63 — completed pre-Issue context work; do not reopen it merely to extend the ongoing-delivery use case.
- #62 — existing Project UX work; its pause and acceptance requirements remain independent.
- #65 — existing real-project dogfood gate; relevant future observations may be linked after separate target/start authorization.
- #42 — execution telemetry Discovery; high-frequency observability is not part of this Issue.

items.body:
## 한국어 요약

Notion 같은 외부 공간을 초기 기획·링크 모음에 한정하지 않고, 개발 중 프로젝트 현황·문제·선택·승인·변경 요청을 관리하는 데 사용하는 경우의 연결 규칙을 정리합니다. GitHub는 저장소 작업의 실행 계약·상태·변경·검증 원본으로 유지합니다.

#63에서 채택한 이슈 이전 맥락 처리의 후속입니다. 기존 규칙을 다시 만들거나 Notion을 필수 의존성으로 넣지 않고, 진행 중 보고 → 사용자 판단 → GitHub 반영 확인 → 실행 결과 전달의 부족한 부분을 검토합니다.

이번 등록은 계획·요구 정리의 첫 단계입니다. 자동화 구현, 저장소 파일 변경, 언어 정책 변경, #62 보류 해제, #65 도그푸딩 개시, v0.1.0 범위 추가 또는 출시 승인을 뜻하지 않습니다. 현행 정책에 따라 이 짧은 한국어 요약과 영어 상세를 함께 둡니다.

## Classification

Bounded Discovery / follow-up to #63. No release milestone is assigned. A decision about placement and scope is the deliverable; connector implementation is not pre-authorized.

## Objective

Decide the smallest tool-independent reporting and decision-handoff contract needed when a maintainer operates a project in an external workspace throughout development, while GitHub remains authoritative for tracked repository work.

The external workspace may own project-level coordination, non-repository work, and the original human decision. It must not independently overwrite GitHub Issue lifecycle or repository contracts. Repository execution must remain usable without Notion or another external service.

## Scope and questions

1. **Ongoing project reporting.** Define which meaningful events warrant a maintainer-facing update: an accepted result, material scope/phase change, blocker, decision request, failed verification, or resolution. Include source links, observation time, relevant revision, uncertainty, and the next meaningful action where applicable. Do not require per-commit reports or copy every Issue status.
2. **Decision requests.** Identify the exact choice, applicable work/revision, options, recommendation and reasons, consequences, material constraints, unanswered questions, and limits on execution/merge/release authority. Avoid a mandatory database or metadata field for every item.
3. **Decision recording and application.** Distinguish a human decision from confirmation that it has reached the authorizing GitHub record. Preserve the decision source, authorized actor, selected option, affected version/scope, and exclusions. A changed request, conflicting instruction, or revoked decision must be reconciled before affected execution resumes. A generic approval is not permission to merge or release.
4. **Failure and consistency.** Cover stale summaries, missing/inaccessible sources, partial reads, write failure after a decision, uncertain mutation outcome, duplicate retries, concurrent human/agent changes, and a result that fails to reach the external summary. Re-read before retrying. Do not convert unavailable data into an empty result or report a failed write as applied. Block affected work when authority/evidence is unresolved; unrelated authorized work may continue under the existing queue rules.
5. **Language ownership.** Compare the maintainer's Notion-centered Korean explanation preference with #58 and the current CONTRIBUTING/template requirement for Korean summaries in GitHub. Propose an explicit disposition; do not silently remove existing Korean or English records or make conflicting translations executable.
6. **Durable evidence for later documents.** Define the minimum references needed to connect requirements, decisions, changes, verification, and delivery to the version being described. Distinguish mutable current summaries from retained decision/evidence snapshots. Do not add seven mandatory report files, raw transcripts, or a document-generation service to the Core Profile.
7. **Placement.** Separate portable workflow semantics, repository-specific contribution guidance, optional external adapters, and Notion page/view design. Repository-only users must not need an external account, database, or reporting runtime.

## Expected result and completion conditions

- Compare the current WORKFLOW_SPEC, CONTRIBUTING, Work/Discovery/PR templates, and relevant outcomes of #58/#63; identify existing coverage before proposing changes.
- Produce a concise responsibility/authority mapping and event-to-report/decision flow, with proposed changes linked to their current source.
- Record a disposition of Adopt, Split, Defer, or Reject. An accepted design is not a claim that an adapter or automatic synchronization works.
- Provide clearly labeled walkthrough evidence for ordinary progress, a human decision, a changed/revoked request, partial write and safe retry, stale/conflicting language, unavailable private evidence, and continuation without the external workspace.
- Identify any independently trackable, separately authorized repository change and any external-workspace-only work. A design decision may complete without implementing an adapter.
- Keep #65's actual-use findings and release-blocking/non-blocking/external-limitation decisions separate. Do not make every proposed convenience a new v0.1.0 release gate.

## Authority and intake

The maintainer requested a work plan and the first stage to begin on 2026-09-25, following the proposal to improve Notion project operations and register this GitHub follow-up. This registration and the initial Notion planning/operating-definition work are within that first stage. Repository implementation, rollout, merge, language-policy replacement, and release require their normal explicit scope/authority path and have not started here.

Intended intake is Backlog in the existing Dedicated User Project, with no milestone, estimate, or release-scope assignment inferred. The current connector does not expose GitHub Projects actions and this session has no configured GitHub CLI. Project membership and actual Status must be established/read back through an authorized supported path before repository execution; this Issue body is not a substitute for Project state and does not claim that attachment succeeded.

## Boundaries

- Preserve existing Issue/PR/Project meanings, independent Review/QA, and separate execution, merge, and release authority.
- No new Notion database, GitHub custom field, cross-repository Project, webhook, scheduler, paid integration, or runtime configuration is created by this Issue.
- Do not copy private workspace pages, personal records, credentials, or raw sessions into this public repository. Use only approved, minimal excerpts and safe references when later evidence is needed.
- Preserve the recorded pauses and prerequisites of #62 and #65. Do not select a dogfood repository, start synthetic work to close #65, request #39 release authority, or publish a tag/Release.

## Related records

- #63 — pre-Issue context and promotion; this follow-up addresses continuing project operations after intake.
- #58 — current language convention.
- #65 — real-project dogfood; existing gates remain unchanged.
- #42 — execution telemetry is a separate concern and is not introduced here.

items.title: [Duplicate of #445] Add ARMv7 cross-build and a minimal embedded dependency profile
items.body:
Parent: #440. Contract dependency: #442 (S0). Can run in parallel with S2 after the minimum target/profile contract; no FPGA hardware is needed for compile and replay tests.

## Outcome

Build the maintained C++ backend for **32-bit ARMv7-A/Cortex-A9 Linux on Zynq-7035**, without requiring Qt, a webview, desktop camera SDKs, Python, GPU inference, or network asset retrieval at application startup. Keep desktop Windows/Linux builds intact.

This is portability and dependency control, not a guarantee that the Cortex-A9 runs the full 5,000-fps scientific pipeline.

## Source starting points

Refresh the source baseline pinned in #440. Inspect `CMakeLists.txt`, `src/backend/CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/MIBOptions.cmake`, `cmake/MIBDependencies.cmake`, `cmake/MIBCompilerSettings.cmake`, `CMakePresets.json`, `conan/profiles/`, `env/`, and backend CI.

Observed baseline:

- `MIB_BUILD_BACKEND_ONLY` already removes the Qt frontend/autogen requirement; preserve it.
- `mib_processing` still combines science with HDF5, frame storage and native-core management; `mib_backend` composes desktop/hardware services.
- MindVision defaults ON, and ONNX Runtime availability can enable dependencies/model checks. Embedded capability selection must not vary accidentally with the build host.
- Linux native-core packaging explicitly recognizes x86_64/aarch64 and otherwise uses the processor string. Audit runtime architecture/fingerprint verification end-to-end for ARMv7; do not merely rename an artifact.

## 1. Reproducible target profile

Add a documented embedded CMake preset/toolchain and matching dependency host/build profiles, with names finalized under repository conventions.

Pin compiler, sysroot, libc/C++ runtime, architecture, float ABI, FPU/NEON settings, package versions and feature selections to the S0 target. Cross-compile on a development/CI host; do not require building all dependencies on the instrument.

Use the existing manifest/profile mechanism as the single source of truth. Do not copy independent package lists into Dockerfiles, scripts and docs. Choose one target sysroot/package provenance strategy and prevent host libraries from entering the target link. Cross-configuration probes cannot silently execute ARM binaries on x86.

Audit ELF machine/class, dynamic dependencies, RPATHs and required symbol versions; produce a dependency/size report and runtime manifest. An AArch64 binary is not acceptable evidence for this issue.

## 2. Explicit embedded feature closure

Make required/optional components selectable consistently at configure, compilation, linking, packaging and runtime-capability layers:

- exclude Qt/frontend, Tauri/webview, Python bindings, Windows packaging and unselected proprietary SDKs;
- exclude ONNX Runtime/model assets unless explicitly enabled for a validated ARM use case;
- make remote telemetry/crash-upload components optional without weakening required local diagnostics;
- retain HDF5/SQLite where needed for the accepted local recording workflow;
- restrict OpenCV to actually used modules in the chosen profile; no speculative claim that all imaging dependencies can already be removed;
- avoid provisioning unused models/datasets or discovering disabled optional dependencies;
- reuse POSIX serial/protocol components as applicable; no mandatory Boost/framework-wide adoption.

If a result-first deployment can omit host processing/playback services, add narrow target/composition seams justified by dependency evidence. Share maintained source and contracts; do not fork `mib_processing` or create a second science implementation. Missing capabilities must remain explicit, not successful stubs for requested hardware.

A native processing-core loader may be disabled for a fixed appliance profile; if enabled, preserve signature, identity, compatibility and lease checks on ARM. Optional means not needed by that profile, not bypassing trust for a required feature.

## 3. ARM32 portability audit

Add regression coverage for:

- fixed-width frame/run IDs, counters and timestamps, including values above 2^32 and 2^53;
- checked dimension/stride/length multiplication before allocation or pointer arithmetic;
- `size_t`/`long`/pointer-width assumptions, alignment and packed-structure access;
- compiler-dependent struct layout at C ABI boundaries; IPC/DMA use explicit encoding, not native layouts;
- large-file offsets and HDF5 files beyond 4 GiB where the recording contract permits them;
- architecture-specific intrinsics, x86 flags and accidental `-march=native`;
- 64-bit atomic correctness/link requirements without assuming lock-free operation on ARM32;
- endianness and float representation where data crosses wire/file boundaries;
- native-core platform strings, manifests and runtime fingerprints when the loader is included.

Use documented scientific tolerances for floating-point comparisons. Do not change golden outputs or enable unsafe floating-point optimizations merely to pass ARM tests.

## 4. CI and evidence levels

1. Keep existing Linux backend/no-Qt and relevant Windows regressions green.
2. Add ARMv7 cross-compile and dependency/ELF audit.
3. Run deterministic contract/science/HDF5 fixture tests under a supported ARM runtime or QEMU, recording exactly which. Emulation is functional evidence, not real-time evidence.
4. When hardware is available, run native tests and the S2 headless workflow on the actual board/BSP.

Include no-network runtime tests with pre-provisioned assets and no Qt/display server. Collect configure/build duration, artifact/installed size, dependency closure, runtime RSS and fixture throughput as measured baselines. Freeze physical budgets under S0 before calling them passing thresholds.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Clean documented build produces ARM32 artifacts against the pinned target sysroot without host-library contamination.
- [ ] The embedded profile configures/builds with Qt, webview, Python, ONNX and unselected SDKs absent.
- [ ] Build capabilities match packaged/runtime capabilities; unsupported required workflows fail explicitly.
- [ ] ARM width/alignment/overflow/large-file regressions pass; enabled native-core trust and identity checks remain fail-closed.
- [ ] Shared scientific and HDF5 fixtures preserve existing semantics within reviewed tolerances.
- [ ] CI distinguishes compile-only, emulated execution and native-board evidence.
- [ ] Desktop regressions remain green and same-PR build/knowledge-map documentation is updated.

## Suggested PR slices

1. Add target profile and compile/ELF audit before changing behavior.
2. Close explicitly disabled dependency/asset leaks with no-desktop-dependency tests.
3. Add ARM32 regression fixes and functional fixture execution.
4. Record native-board measurements and integrate the headless acceptance workflow.

**Non-goals:** changing algorithms, replacing all libraries, guaranteeing raw acquisition/storage throughput, or implementing a touchscreen/FPGA transport in this issue.

items.title: [Duplicate of #443] Freeze Zynq-7035 target, execution boundaries, capabilities and resource budgets
items.body:
Parent: #440.

## Outcome

Create the reviewed architecture and target manifest needed to make small, testable changes now without guessing the final board or building a second MIB application.

**Priority/order:** first contract milestone. No implementation dependency. S1/S2 and mock S3/S4 work can begin from an accepted subset; final board-dependent acceptance requires resolved hardware fields.

## Baseline to inspect

Start from the pinned source review in #440 (`develop` at `2fe02824de3a72114b7c7d5a3a2af46a6cc64b95`) and refresh it before execution.

Read `AGENTS.md`, `knowledge_map/Agent-Onboarding.md`, `docs/golden-principles.md`, and existing ADR/plan conventions. Inspect:

- `CMakeLists.txt`, `src/backend/CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/MIBOptions.cmake`, `cmake/MIBDependencies.cmake`, `cmake/MIBCompilerSettings.cmake`, `CMakePresets.json`, and dependency/profile manifests;
- `AppBackend`, `BackendFacade`, `ExperimentCoordinator`, readiness/run configuration, discovery/startup policy, recording/accounting and memory-budget interfaces;
- current bridge schema and #372 implementation/evidence;
- #337, #349–#357, #423 and their exact firmware handoffs.

The existing Qt-free backend is the starting point, not work to recreate. Inventory implemented-on-branch, merged, released, mock-tested, ARM-tested and hardware-qualified states separately.

## 1. Target manifest

Record, with provenance and explicit `unknown` entries rather than defaults:

| Area | Required fields |
|---|---|
| SoC/board | XC7Z035 board/module, schematic revision, package/speed grade, carrier, boot straps and relevant pin allocation |
| CPU/software | ARMv7-A/Cortex-A9, 32-bit ABI, endianness, float ABI/FPU settings, compiler/sysroot/libc, BSP/kernel/bootloader versions |
| Memory | Installed/usable DDR, reserved/CMA regions, DMA/addressability limits, framebuffer allocation and measured shared-memory bandwidth |
| Storage | Boot and data media, capacity/endurance, local filesystem, removable-media behavior, measured sustained writes/flush latency |
| Sensor/FPGA | Exact sensor/ingress, pin/clock/transceiver compatibility, firmware/interface bundle, result/control/preview channels |
| Display | 7-inch 1024×600 candidate, exact LCD model, RGB pinout/voltage/timing, controller/scanout path, pixel format and refresh rate |
| Touch | Exact touch controller, I2C/USB/other bus, reset/IRQ, voltage, driver, orientation/calibration, multitouch behavior |
| Instrument safety | Output-safe states, physical inhibit/E-stop path, watchdog behavior, pump/focus/trigger devices and reset sequence |

Do not assume the 50-pin RGB connector includes a known touch interface, the ARM CPU exposes a compatible display output directly, or a successful KU5P design fits the Zynq. Consume the exact-device feasibility evidence owned by #423; do not duplicate its scientific study.

## 2. Ownership and execution map

For every operator-critical capability map current source owner → accepted shared contract → embedded implementation → evidence/gap.

Cover discovery, settings persistence, apply/readback, readiness, background/calibration, experiment start/stop, frame/result accounting, processing identity, trigger timing, local recording, review/export, faults and shutdown.

Freeze these responsibilities:

- `AppBackend`/shared coordinator owns one authoritative lifecycle and hardware authorization.
- FPGA owns the sorting-critical pipeline/timing required by the accepted deadline; software reference/replay and any ARM-side processing are explicitly identified and budgeted.
- Device transports hide OS/driver/register details behind narrow adapters; neither UI nor application-domain code owns raw device pointers.
- Local UI and CLI call the same facade semantics; the daemon is the only hardware owner in appliance mode.
- Desktop and embedded builds share maintained source, contracts and tests, not necessarily renderer, transport or all optional services.

Record any remaining shell-owned startup/configuration/finalization policy as a specific extraction, with current owner and regression. Do not create a second coordinator, another universal plugin framework, or parallel science code.

## 3. Capability/deployment profiles

Specify a minimal profile model, using existing build/configuration mechanisms where possible. Distinguish:

- desktop Host SDK;
- explicit mock/replay development;
- embedded Zynq FPGA-result appliance.

Capabilities must describe actual acquisition path, required metrics, local recording modes, preview/background support, peripheral availability, CPU/offline processing and diagnostics. Build-time exclusion, runtime unavailable, unsupported and unhealthy are different states.

Keep public contract units/identities stable. Native CPU plugin ABI, application IPC schema and FPGA register/result/DMA schema are independent version domains. Unsupported scientific metrics remain absent; profile compatibility may not silently downgrade an experiment.

## 4. Resource and timing budget contract

Define numeric targets before qualification; unknown hardware limits block the affected physical gate rather than becoming invented passing thresholds.

Budget separately:

- sensor ingress throughput and exposure/event-to-physical-trigger deadline;
- FPGA processing/results and maximum objects/contours per frame;
- PS↔PL result and preview traffic, batching, IRQ/CPU load and DDR contention;
- OS/backend/UI/driver/CMA/stack/cache/queue memory, with safety headroom;
- local persistence backlog, sustained writes, flush/finalization latency and recording policy;
- sampled preview/display refresh, UI input latency, boot-to-ready and reconnect/shutdown bounds.

Raw 512×96 Mono8 at 5,000 fps is 245.76 MB/s by calculation. This is a sizing input only. Do not assume full raw recording, every-frame CPU processing, or frontend rendering at acquisition rate.

Declare result-loss and overload policies explicitly. Required loss cannot masquerade as a clean Complete. UI sampling is a separate intentional policy. Reuse #368/#370 time/validity/byte-budget concepts.

## 5. Failure-policy decisions

Freeze backend-owned client-disconnect policy: baseline controlled Stop & Save; unattended continuation requires an explicitly validated method. Rendering pause/navigation is not loss of the controller session.

Specify independent UI-process, daemon-process, Linux-hang, FPGA-fault and power-loss cases. Backend crash/reboot must leave outputs inhibited and require explicit re-arm. Define boot-time incomplete-run recovery without promising that an arbitrary partially written HDF5 file is recoverable.

## Deliverables / acceptance

- [ ] Architecture ADR and execution plan under `docs/decisions/` and `docs/exec-plans/active/`, using repository naming conventions and a status/decision log.
- [ ] Machine-readable target/capability manifest with provenance, resolved fields and explicit blockers.
- [ ] Source/evidence inventory and narrow extraction list linked to existing owners/issues.
- [ ] Reviewed ARM/FPGA/UI/driver/persistence boundary and version-domain map.
- [ ] Numeric budget/acceptance template populated where measurable; no fabricated hardware limits.
- [ ] Mock-first and physical qualification gates clearly separated, including #423 dependencies.
- [ ] Small PR sequence and cross-repository firmware/driver ownership handoff recorded.
- [ ] Matching knowledge-map/build/threading/data-flow updates and documentation checks.

**Non-goals:** actual full board port, new algorithm selection, scientific threshold migration, desktop shell replacement, or claiming physical feasibility from architecture diagrams.
