items.title: [Duplicate of #441] Standalone MIB instrument on Zynq-7035: headless backend + local touchscreen
items.body:
## Outcome

Prepare and deploy MIB Studio as a **fully standalone instrument on Zynq-7035**, with the ARM processing system running the authoritative C++ application backend and a local touchscreen acting only as a presentation client. Normal startup, configuration, experiment execution, safe stopping, persistence, and review must not require a PC, browser on another device, Internet connection, or cloud login.

This is an incremental platform/product workstream, not a replacement backend or a wholesale desktop rewrite.

## Target and boundaries

- User-selected processor family: **Zynq-7035 / XC7Z035, dual-core Cortex-A9, 32-bit ARMv7-A Linux**. Do not substitute an AArch64 target, Zynq UltraScale+, or KU5P/MicroBlaze.
- Touchscreen candidate: **7-inch, 1024×600, capacitive touch, advertised 50-pin parallel RGB**. Exact panel/touch-controller part numbers, pinout, voltages, timing, and board display path remain unverified.
- Exact board/module, package/speed grade, RAM, boot/storage devices, BSP, sensor connection, and display/touch drivers are open hardware-manifest fields. Software preparation can proceed against explicit mocks; physical acceptance cannot pass with these fields unresolved.
- IMX426/KU5P work is reusable development evidence, not proof that its RTL, interfaces, performance, or transport fit XC7Z035. Do not silently import the MindVision→KU5P PCIe deployment from #349 as the on-chip Zynq transport.
- No new Qt dependency in the embedded backend or touchscreen. Preserve the existing desktop Qt shell during migration. React/Tauri desktop work remains separate; do not assume a webview is the right embedded renderer.

Hardware reference: [AMD Zynq 7000 family and device table](https://www.amd.com/en/products/adaptive-socs-and-fpgas/soc/zynq-7000.html). Exact board documentation and the BSP/toolchain must additionally be pinned by the target-manifest issue.

## Source-reviewed baseline — not execution evidence

Reviewed `develop` at `2fe02824de3a72114b7c7d5a3a2af46a6cc64b95` on 2026-09-22. No ARM build or hardware validation is claimed by this specification.

- [Root CMake](https://github.com/gavinlouuu-kpt/mib-studio-qt/blob/2fe02824de3a72114b7c7d5a3a2af46a6cc64b95/CMakeLists.txt) already gates Qt autogen/frontend under `MIB_BUILD_BACKEND_ONLY`.
- [Backend targets](https://github.com/gavinlouuu-kpt/mib-studio-qt/blob/2fe02824de3a72114b7c7d5a3a2af46a6cc64b95/src/backend/CMakeLists.txt) already separate `mib_processing` and `mib_backend`, but the portable processing target still includes processing, HDF5, buffering, playback, and native-core support. Qt-free is not the same as a minimal embedded dependency closure.
- [Dependencies](https://github.com/gavinlouuu-kpt/mib-studio-qt/blob/2fe02824de3a72114b7c7d5a3a2af46a6cc64b95/cmake/MIBDependencies.cmake) discover OpenCV and optional ONNX Runtime, and contain SDK/platform paths. [Build options](https://github.com/gavinlouuu-kpt/mib-studio-qt/blob/2fe02824de3a72114b7c7d5a3a2af46a6cc64b95/cmake/MIBOptions.cmake) default MindVision ON. Embedded features must be selected intentionally, not by whatever dependencies happen to be installed on the build machine.
- [AppBackend](https://github.com/gavinlouuu-kpt/mib-studio-qt/blob/2fe02824de3a72114b7c7d5a3a2af46a6cc64b95/include/backend/app/AppBackend.h) owns services and ordered shutdown. It already exposes experiment/discovery and injected LUT networking; startup discovery is currently started by the shell. Audit lifecycle policy rather than rebuilding it.
- [BackendFacade](https://github.com/gavinlouuu-kpt/mib-studio-qt/blob/2fe02824de3a72114b7c7d5a3a2af46a6cc64b95/include/backend/app/BackendFacade.h) already provides typed commands and operation tracking. Extend this authority and existing bridge contracts; do not create independent readiness or experiment logic in the embedded UI.

Refresh these SHAs and implementation status at execution time. An issue checkbox is not evidence that code is absent or completed.

## Architecture decision

```text
Local touchscreen client       CLI / test client
          |                          |
          +---- versioned local API -+
                         |
               headless instrument host
                         |
              AppBackend / BackendFacade
                         |
      shared experiment/readiness/configuration authority
            |                 |                  |
       local storage     device services    FPGA-result adapter
       HDF5 / SQLite      pump/focus/etc.          |
                                      Linux driver + PS↔PL transport
                                                 |
                                  FPGA acquisition/processing/timing
```

One C++ application backend owns experiment lifecycle, validation, configuration, result accounting, persistence, and hardware authorization. FPGA logic owns the accepted sorting-critical pixel/decision/trigger path where required by the measured deadline. ARM performs supervision and any explicitly budgeted processing; Linux/UI timing must not silently become the hard real-time trigger source.

Keep host-frame and FPGA-result paths distinct. FPGA results must not be wrapped in fake `ICamera::grabFrame()` frames or forced through a second full-frame CPU processing pipeline. Share domain contracts and orchestration where valid, not an artificial common transport.

The local UI is a separate process over a narrow API so it can restart and reconnect without destroying the backend. Existing desktop in-process adapters may remain. This is one deployed backend instance, not an RPC server running alongside a competing in-process hardware owner.

## Non-negotiable behavior

1. Backend Start revalidates readiness and freezes run/configuration/algorithm/firmware identities; UI readiness is only a projection. Device reconnect or firmware/configuration changes invalidate stale readiness.
2. UI navigation, slow rendering, paused preview, client disconnect, or restart cannot create unbounded retention, stop persistence implicitly, or authorize hardware. Client-loss handling follows an explicit backend policy; baseline is controlled Stop & Save unless a validated method explicitly permits unattended continuation.
3. A separate hardware/PL watchdog and physical inhibit strategy handles backend/OS failure. Screen buttons and software Stop are not an emergency stop. No automatic re-arming after crash, reboot, or update.
4. Preview is bounded/sampled and separate from required result retention. Required result loss and deliberate preview replacement are separately accounted.
5. Preserve scientific contracts, legacy HDF5 reads, units, timestamp clock domains, validity, calibration, and provenance. Unavailable metrics are absent, never fabricated zeros.
6. Results-first recording is the baseline for the FPGA appliance. Full raw recording requires an independent measured throughput/storage gate. At the previously discussed 512×96 Mono8 / 5,000 fps target, raw payload alone is 245.76 MB/s by calculation; this is not an achieved rate or a promise about onboard storage.
7. Required assets/configuration remain local and version-pinned. Update/telemetry/NAS/MLflow/Biowork access is optional at runtime; an outage cannot block safe operation or finalization.
8. Desktop Windows/Linux workflows and accepted reliability checks remain supported throughout.

## Existing work to reuse — do not duplicate or close by implication

| Work | Relationship |
|---|---|
| #246, #372 | Single-backend/presentation separation; reuse facade, integer/frame contracts, bounded client behavior. Embedded shell is not a mandate to finish or replace all Tauri work. |
| #371, #369, #368, #370 | Reliability, readiness, clock/validity semantics, byte budgets. Consume accepted checkpoints and implement only measured missing seams. |
| #419 | Shared backend discovery/startup policy. Do not add touchscreen-owned discovery. |
| #337 | Existing full FPGA pipeline work; reconcile firmware ownership and remaining functionality. |
| #349–#357 | Result-first acquisition, capability/provenance concepts and transport tests; KU5P PCIe specifics are not the Zynq PS↔PL implementation. |
| #301, #394 | Scientific/native processing contracts; an in-process CPU plugin ABI is not a DMA/IPC wire format. |
| #423 | Scientific selection and exact-XC7Z035 feasibility gates. This epic does not select absdiff/U-Net/Laplacian by default or bypass those gates. |
| #397, #399 | Optional downstream analysis/integration; not dependencies of local instrument operation. |

## Workstreams and dependency order

Linked implementation issues will cover:

- **S0 — Target manifest, ownership inventory, capability profiles and budgets.** Establish the architecture/acceptance contract first; unknown board facts remain explicit.
- **S1 — ARMv7 cross-build and embedded dependency profile.** Can start with compile/replay evidence before hardware arrives.
- **S2 — Headless instrument host, versioned local API and CLI.** Develop against the existing backend and mocks after the minimum S0 contract.
- **S3 — Zynq FPGA-result/control adapter and hardware handoff.** Fake/replay tests first; physical integration requires exact board/interface evidence and the relevant #423 checkpoint.
- **S4 — Lightweight touchscreen client and display/touch bring-up.** Prototype against S2 contracts; evaluate LVGL first without committing the core to a UI toolkit.
- **S5 — Appliance image, persistence/recovery and end-to-end qualification.** Integrate the accepted S1–S4 slices; final physical acceptance also requires the applicable scientific/FPGA gates.

S1/S2 and S3/S4 mock work may proceed in parallel after their specific interface contracts are accepted. Do not block every task on every historical epic, or declare full standalone acceptance from a mock UI.

## First useful milestone

On desktop Linux, run the same accepted C++ backend with **no Qt or display server**, drive configure → readiness → fixed-count mock run → stop/finalize → reopen HDF5 through the CLI/local API, and demonstrate client restart/reconnection with correct run accounting. Then cross-build and run the same fixtures on ARMv7. This precedes a full touchscreen transplant or FPGA algorithm rewrite.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Child issues are linked with dependencies, code starting points, regression tests, and explicit physical-vs-mock gates.
- [ ] Target manifest and ADR/execution plan are committed under repository conventions.
- [ ] One reproducible ARMv7 build/image has an audited embedded dependency closure and no Qt/webview runtime requirement.
- [ ] CLI and local touchscreen consume one backend-owned lifecycle through versioned, bounded contracts.
- [ ] Zynq hardware/interface compatibility, driver ownership, configuration commit, result decoding and watchdog behavior are physically qualified.
- [ ] Local operator can boot, configure, inspect readiness, run, safely stop/save, reopen, and export without a PC or network.
- [ ] UI failures, missing storage, result overflow, firmware mismatch, backend crash and power interruption never produce false completion or unintended actuation.
- [ ] Declared RAM/CPU/DDR/storage/display/latency budgets pass on the exact board under combined load; end-to-end trigger timing is measured physically.
- [ ] Scientific/firmware/app/configuration identities and required loss accounting survive recording and review.
- [ ] Desktop regressions, cross-platform conformance, rollback, operator documentation, and reproducible evidence pass.

Implementation must follow `AGENTS.md`, `docs/golden-principles.md`, regression-first tests, and same-PR `knowledge_map` updates. This issue authorizes planning and incremental implementation scopes, not a claim that the port or hardware is already working.

items.body:
## Work item

- Work ID: `S2.2-Chevalley-Cor2`
- Queue state: `READY`
- Canonical branch: `work/s2-2-chevalley-cor2`
- Source: Chapter 1 §2.2, Corollary 2, printed p.7 / uploaded PDF p.17
- Ownership: unclaimed until a B/C/D/E worker creates the canonical branch

## Source boundary

Independent source check fixes the immediate second corollary: a quadratic form over the finite field `K` in at least three variables has a nonzero zero. The source treats this as a specialization of Corollary 1 to a homogeneous polynomial of degree `2`: homogeneity gives vanishing at the origin, and `2 < n` when there are at least three variables.

No book prose/image should be committed.

## Dependency state

The real upstream is Corollary 1, canonical work item #70 / PR #80. That work is now DONE on `main`, so the implementation gate is open. The later duplicate scheduler issue #84 is closed as duplicate and is not a dependency.

## Intended implementation boundary

- use the project Corollary 1 theorem from #70 rather than duplicating its cardinality argument;
- choose a source-faithful representation of an `n`-variable quadratic form and only the adapter needed to the polynomial statement expected by #70;
- preserve the exact hypothesis “at least three variables” without adding unnecessary nonsingularity or nondegeneracy assumptions;
- add independent Blueprint explanation + declaration linkage;
- run policy, `lake build`, `lake exe vbp build`, self-review and merge.

## Theorem-strength rule

Do not close the target with a ready-made finite-field isotropy theorem that already implies the corollary. General polynomial/quadratic-form infrastructure is allowed.

items.body:
## Parent

#943 — concise agent-readable gate decision surface.

Roadmap slice: #945 C6.2. Depends on finalized outcome enforcement, TaskLedger, CiSpineContract, and typed ReviewJudgment.

## Objective

Define one machine-readable terminal decision artifact that lets a coding agent or maintainer identify the blocking next action without reconstructing workflow logs.

## Contract

```text
GateDecisionSummary
  RevisionIdentity / review semantics
  PASS | FAIL | NOT_PROVEN
  blocking deterministic evidence[]
  unavailable Required evidence[]
  material reviewer actions[]
  nonblocking review/infrastructure degradation[]
  exact reproduction or retry actions[]
  confirmed inline delivery refs[]
  artifact/receipt bundle refs[]
  stable coordinator/tool identity?
```

## Scope

- Derive the structured summary only from FinalizedOutcome, spine/task consumers, terminal receipts, ReviewJudgment, and confirmed delivery receipts.
- Require exact receipt/current-revision links for every blocker/gap/action.
- Include reproduction only for approved tasks that executed, or a bounded retry path for unavailable Required infrastructure.
- Link rather than duplicate confirmed inline findings.
- Separate code failure, evidence unavailable, review limitation, provider degradation, and delivery failure.
- Define deterministic value ordering and size bounds that cannot drop blocking evidence.
- Add schema/version/verifier.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every FAIL has a current-revision deterministic receipt and bounded next action.
- [ ] Every NOT_PROVEN names the exact Required gap and retry/owner path without accusing code.
- [ ] Unexecuted optional proof never becomes a command for the maintainer.
- [ ] Confirmed inline findings are referenced once.
- [ ] Provider/model degradation is nonblocking when the deterministic spine suffices.
- [ ] PASS does not claim optional model/review completeness.
- [ ] Model-off summaries are complete.
- [ ] Stale/forged/mismatched refs fail verification.

## Proof

- PASS, deterministic FAIL, Required timeout/unavailable, mixed finding+gap, provider outage, delivery failure and model-off goldens.
- Confirmed inline/no-duplication and no-homework fixtures.
- Reproduction/retry validation and stale/forged negatives.
- Size/value degradation tests.
- Full gate/task/review/delivery/verifier/workspace/fmt/Clippy/policy.

## Non-goals

- No Markdown/GitHub rendering; sibling C6.3.
- No outcome computation.
- No automatic repair/merge.
- No GitHub check publication.

## Rollback

Retain exact blocking receipt data in the finalized artifact and disable the structured projection; never collapse FAIL/NOT_PROVEN distinctions.

items.title: Duplicate of #37: ergodicity alone does not imply the O(ε) volatility-smile correction
items.body:
The [any-equation page](https://homogenization.microprediction.org/any-equation.html) says “Sircar and Papanicolaou (1999) derive it for **any fast ergodic volatility driver**.” The [survey](https://homogenization.microprediction.org/survey.html) says they derive “this first-order smile for **any fast ergodic driver**, including a Markov chain.” Ergodicity alone is insufficient for the displayed \(O(\varepsilon)\) Green–Kubo variance-convexity correction.

The cited authors’ [1999 paper, §§2.2–2.4 and 3.3](https://math.stanford.edu/~papanico/pubftp/stochvol.pdf) separates the **uncorrelated** volatility-mixture calculation from the correlated stochastic-volatility PDE. Its fast-scale smile calculation uses an averaging/**central limit** theorem under conditions on the driver (see its §3.3), which cannot follow from ergodicity alone. Correlation with the stock-price shock can also yield an \(O(\sqrt\varepsilon)\) leverage term, as this site’s fast-factor example itself shows.

### Stationary ergodic driver with no finite Green–Kubo coefficient

Let \(Y_t=U+t/\varepsilon\pmod{2\pi}\), with \(U\) uniform on the circle, and take variance \(v(Y)=v_0+\delta\cos Y>0\). This continuous-time rotation flow is stationary and ergodic, but its centered covariance is
\[
C(s)=\frac{\delta^2}{2}\cos(s/\varepsilon),
\]
which does not have a convergent one-sided Green–Kubo integral. The actual integrated variance is
\[
V_t=v_0t+\delta\varepsilon[\sin(U+t/\varepsilon)-\sin U],\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(V_t)=\delta^2\varepsilon^2[1-\cos(t/\varepsilon)].
\]
With stock-price Brownian noise independent of \(U\), the Hull–White mixture \(\mathbb E[C_{\rm BS}(V_t)]\) has a leading fluctuating-variance correction of order \(\varepsilon^2\), with oscillatory coefficient, **not** the universally asserted \(O(\varepsilon)\) term \(tK\partial_V^2 C_{\rm BS}\). This does not challenge the site’s finite irreducible Markov-chain theorem: those chains mix exponentially and have a finite \(K\).

**Suggested correction:** restrict the Sircar–Papanicolaou attribution to uncorrelated drivers satisfying the covariance integrability/CLT conditions needed for this specific correction. Say finite irreducible Markov chains are an example. Keep correlated fast-factor skew as a separate case, with its potentially earlier \(O(\sqrt\varepsilon)\) term.

## Work item

- Work ID: `S2.2-Chevalley-Cor1`
- Queue state after scheduler activation: `READY`
- Canonical branch: `work/s2-2-chevalley-cor1`
- Source: Chapter 1 §2.2, Corollary 1, printed p.7 / uploaded PDF p.17

## Source boundary

Independent source check fixes the target immediately after Theorem 3 (Chevalley–Warning): for finitely many `n`-variable polynomials `f_α` over the finite field `K`, if `∑ deg(f_α) < n` and every `f_α(0)=0`, then the common zero locus contains a point other than `0`.

The source proof is the one-line cardinality contradiction: if the common-zero set were exactly `{0}`, then its cardinality would be `1`, contradicting Theorem 3's divisibility/congruence by the characteristic prime.

No book prose/image should be committed.

## Dependency conclusion

The core Chevalley–Warning theorem #52 / PR #68 is DONE on main, so there is no remaining project gate. This item may be implemented end-to-end directly from current main.

## Intended boundary

- reuse the project #52 common-zero cardinality theorem rather than mathlib's ready-made Chevalley–Warning theorem;
- state the origin-vanishing hypothesis without silently strengthening homogeneity assumptions;
- prove existence of a nonzero common zero by the source cardinality contradiction;
- add independent Blueprint explanation and declaration linkage;
- policy / `lake build` / `lake exe vbp build`, self-review, merge, and progress sync.

## Theorem-strength rule

Do not close this corollary by invoking a ready-made mathlib theorem whose conclusion is already the existence of a nontrivial common zero. General finite-set/cardinality logic is allowed.

items.title: Historical duplicate of PERF008/#496 — Post-C′ Bytecode continuation hot-path characterization
items.body:
## Independent follow-up

**Origin:** PERF006-D3 / #487 retained structural diagnostics
**Relationship to PERF006:** non-blocking follow-up; PERF008 is **not** required for PERF006 closure
**Initial state:** READY / AUDIT_FIRST
**Nature:** measurement and causal characterization first; no pre-authorized production optimization

## Trigger

PERF006-D3B retained the first current post-C′ structural profile of the real repository workload `bin/protos test --jobs 2` on exact Protos revision `4a03efc15620b37b2e418b3df30b4a26486446ec`, Graal/Truffle 25.3.4.1 / JDK 25.0.4.1.

The historical replay bottleneck is gone: `java.util.HashMap$KeyIterator.next` fell from 92.201% of historical JFR execution samples to 0%, `main` concentration fell from 98.530% to 39.411481%, the retired `compactCompletedChildExecution()` / `invocationActivations.keySet().removeIf(...)` path is statically absent, and current JFR recorded only 191 `jdk.Deoptimization` plus 6 Truffle deoptimizations versus roughly 1.824M of each historically.

The current profile instead exposes a new dominant post-cutover frame:

```text
com.guillermomolina.protos.execution.ProtosBytecodeRootNodeGen$CachedBytecodeNode.continueAt
2736 / 8292 ExecutionSample events = 32.995658%
```

Several generated Builder/materialization frames are also prominent:

```text
Builder$RootStackElement.finalizeExceptionHandlerLocalCounts   7.187651%
Builder.afterChild                                             3.485287%
Builder.beforeChild                                            2.580801%
Builder.beginFinallyHandler                                    2.219006%
Builder.emitLoadLocal                                          1.531597%
```

This is a **new post-C′ optimization opportunity**, not evidence that PERF006 failed and not a reason to extend PERF006 indefinitely.

## Goal

Determine what the `continueAt` / generated-Builder sample concentration actually represents, which part is unavoidable Bytecode DSL continuation execution versus repeated materialization/build work, and whether a bounded production optimization is justified.

Do not assume from top-frame percentage alone that `continueAt` itself is defective.

## Required audit questions

1. On which current workloads does `CachedBytecodeNode.continueAt` remain dominant after warmup?
2. How much sampled cost is actual resumed continuation execution versus Bytecode root creation/materialization/building?
3. Why are generated `Builder.*` frames significant during the Test Tool workload: expected one-time source preparation, repeated root creation, cache miss, context/process isolation cost, or another mechanism?
4. Are roots/bytecodes being rebuilt more frequently than required by current semantic ownership?
5. Does the cost scale with fresh Process count, source count, Task/Future suspension count, call depth, or test count?
6. Are current guest roots compiling/inlining as expected on the affected paths?
7. Are any current invalidation/compilation-failure patterns causally related, rather than merely textual TraceCompilation noise?
8. Is there a mechanical optimization already dictated by ratified C′/Bytecode ownership, or would remediation require a new durable cache/lifetime/context architecture decision?

## Evidence baseline

Authoritative PERF006-D3 evidence is retained in `guillermomolina/protos-benchmarks` at:

```text
D3 evidence commit = ecfa8fb3a23f5661524b7eb812e16e75c833ed7c

```

The D3 diagnostic wall time of 77.613 s is diagnostic context only. It is not an absolute comparator to the historical ~471.985 s run.

## Initial decomposition

### PERF008-A — current hot-path attribution audit

Reproduce/expand the current profile on exact current revisions and separate continuation execution, Bytecode construction/materialization, Process/Test Tool setup and compiler behavior. No production change.

### PERF008-B — candidate comparison / decision gate if needed

If A exposes more than one durable lifetime/cache/materialization architecture, compare alternatives for future durability, scalability, memory behavior, Process/Actor isolation, Graal/Truffle optimizer compatibility and Protos philosophy, then route any substantive architecture choice through the appropriate PLATxxx/Dxxx approval before implementation.

### PERF008-C — bounded remediation

Only if A/B establish a justified optimization. Preserve Protos-visible semantics and C′ continuation ownership.

- do not reintroduce evaluator replay or the retired `compactCompletedChildExecution()` machinery;

```text
planned
```

# TASK-055: Model API failure handling and budget guard

- **type:** feature
- **priority:** P1
- **status:** READY
- **execution_mode:** auto
- **owner (area):** agent
- **depends_on:** TASK-022
- **human_authorization:** no

## Objective

Handle the ways a model provider fails -- rate limits, timeouts, malformed responses, quota exhaustion -- with bounded retry, provider rotation through the existing `orchestrator/routing/` pool, and a hard budget stop.

The budget is ~USD 300 across four projects. A runaway loop can spend it in an afternoon, so the guard must be a hard stop, not a warning.

## Allowed paths

```
agent/runtime/resilience.py
```

## Forbidden paths

```
frontend/**
detection/**
backend/**
agent/runtime/loop.py
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each failure mode has a distinct, tested behaviour -- no bare catch-all.
- [ ] Retries are bounded with backoff and never unbounded.
- [ ] Exhausting one provider's quota rotates to the next and logs a `ROUTING_EVENT`.
- [ ] Reaching the budget ceiling stops further calls rather than warning and continuing.
- [ ] Every failure and rotation lands in the usage ledger.

## Tests required

`tests/unit/` per failure mode against a stubbed transport, including the budget-ceiling stop.

## Documentation requirements

Update `agent/runtime/README.md` and `orchestrator/policies/provider-pool.yaml` notes.

items.title: Postgres health check Unhealthy: TLS handshake to PostgreSQL times out on connector open (duplicate of #5314)

labels.name: sev:L
labels.description: Low - cosmetic, rare edge case, or developer-only

items.body:
**What is failing**

The `PostgreSql` health check on the memex-cloud portal reported Unhealthy: opening a new Npgsql connector stalled in TLS negotiation (`TaskCanceledException` in `SslStream.ForceAuthenticationAsync` → `NpgsqlConnector.NegotiateEncryption`) and the check's cancellation token fired at ~6.5s.

**Probable cause**

Medium confidence — a transient network/TLS handshake delay to the PostgreSQL host exceeded the health check's timeout budget on the first pooled connector open of that window. The stack runs entirely through Npgsql and the `HealthChecks.NpgSql` library; no application frame is implicated.

**Already known — likely duplicate**

This is the same defect as [MeshWeaver#5314](https://github.com/Systemorph/MeshWeaver/issues/5314) (incident `Admin/_LogIncident/b2cc907bf65c0478`): same log site, exception type and top frame, same pod `memex-portal-deployment-5c444645f8-8pdzb`, and this occurrence (14:44:41) falls two minutes after that incident's last sample (14:42:39). This ticket can likely be closed as a duplicate, but a human should confirm the burst at 13:42–14:44 UTC is fully covered by the earlier issue.

**Impact**

Single occurrence on a single portal pod; at most a momentary readiness blip, no user-facing failure evidenced.

**Where to look**

- `HealthChecks.NpgSql.NpgSqlHealthCheck.CheckHealthAsync` (AspNetCore.Diagnostics.HealthChecks) — health check entry point.
- Npgsql connector open path: `Npgsql.Internal.NpgsqlConnector.Open` / `NegotiateEncryption`.
- Pod→Postgres network/TLS latency around 2026-09-22 14:44 UTC; consider health check timeout vs. `NpgsqlTimeout`.

---

### Evidence

| | |
|---|---|
| Fingerprint | `c9defbf7ce85d8f9` |

items.body:
## Parent

#810 — rollback and break-glass authority.

Roadmap slice: #945 E5.2. Depends on stable coordinator/gate authority, RevisionIdentity, CiSpineContract, FinalizedOutcome, and repository governance policy.

## Objective

Define a narrowly scoped, explicit, time-bounded override contract for genuine emergencies without turning NOT_PROVEN or a failing Required obligation into an undocumented pass.

## Contract

A versioned `BreakGlassAuthorization` should bind at least:

```text
repository / PR / exact head or merge-result RevisionIdentity
stable coordinator/check identity
original PASS | FAIL | NOT_PROVEN result and exact blockers/gaps
reason / incident / business justification
allowed action and explicitly excluded actions
required approvers and threshold
approval identities/timestamps/evidence
created / expires / used-at timestamps
mandatory compensating controls
mandatory post-merge rerun deadline
owner / rollback / review record
artifact digest / signature or trusted-source identity
```

## Scope

- Define request, approval, active, used, expired, revoked, rejected, and fulfilled/violated states.
- Require repository-configured approver identities/roles and threshold; self-approval and candidate-controlled approval are prohibited.
- Bind authorization to one exact revision and one original stable result.
- Keep the original FAIL/NOT_PROVEN evidence visible; the override is a separate governance decision, not a rewritten result.
- Define maximum duration/use count, revocation, replay protection, and immutable audit trail.
- Require compensating controls and post-merge rerun obligations appropriate to the overridden evidence.
- Add independent verifier and reason tokens.
- No live GitHub publication/merge behavior in this PR.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Override cannot change the underlying FinalizedOutcome or erase blockers/gaps.
- [ ] Wrong/stale revision, coordinator/check, result, approver, threshold, expiry, use count, or artifact identity fails closed.
- [ ] Self/candidate approval and mutable head-controlled policy cannot authorize an override.
- [ ] Expired/revoked/used authorization cannot be replayed.
- [ ] Required compensating controls and post-merge rerun are explicit and nonempty.
- [ ] Authorization is scope-limited and cannot silently waive unrelated obligations.
- [ ] Every transition is append-only and independently verifiable.
- [ ] Model/provider output has no approval authority.

## Proof

- Complete state/transition/threshold/expiry/use/revocation truth table.
- Wrong/stale revision/result/check/approver and self-approval negatives.
- Replay, mutation, missing compensating control/rerun and scope-escape cases.
- Serialization/signature-or-trusted-source/verifier tests.
- Governance/config/workspace/fmt/Clippy/policy validation.

## Non-goals

- No live check/merge integration; sibling E5.3.
- No automatic approval or emergency classification.
- No branch-protection mutation.
- No weakening of CiSpineContract.

## Rollback

Disable break-glass entirely and require normal stable PASS or manual branch-protection/governance action outside UB Review. Never accept an unverifiable override.

## Parent

Roadmap slice: #945 C2.3. Depends on #861 scheduler and #862 estimate/release children.

## Objective

Replace one undifferentiated timeout with explicit product-level deadline phases.

## Deadline model

```text
first-signal target
decision target
optional-admission stop
finalization reserve boundary
hard kill wall
```

## Scope

- Define typed deadline configuration/state/transitions and monotonic validation.
- Expose current phase to scheduler and model-stage planning.
- Before optional stop, admit value-ranked work normally.
- After optional stop, admit only short high-value work that safely fits policy.
- At finalization boundary, stop all new execution and preserve receipt drain/reconsideration/final lead/delivery/cleanup.
- At hard wall, kill/terminalize hung work.
- Record exact boundary/reason on every defer/cancel/timeout.
- Keep live zero-pending drain for sibling C2.4.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Boundary ordering is validated and impossible configurations fail closed.
- [ ] Required work and finalization reserve cannot be silently consumed by optional tasks.

items.title: RoutingGrain back-pressure episode on memex pod: 36-deep destination queue (duplicate of fleet-wide #1172)
items.body:
**What is failing**

`MeshWeaver.Hosting.Orleans.RoutingGrain` crossed its 64 in-flight dispatch threshold on the memex pod. The episode (`c0d85529#1`) shows 64 dispatches in flight with 4 stream destinations queued and a deepest per-destination queue of 36, with the crossing target `portal/nodeops-…` — the classic head-of-line shape: over half the in-flight slots are held behind legs queued on a small number of slow destinations.

**Probable cause** (moderate confidence)

Same mechanism as the fleet-wide RoutingGrain saturation already filed: a dispatch slot is held from dispatch until the leg terminates, including the unbounded wait for a ThreadPool thread, and legs queued behind one slow destination accumulate in a per-destination queue (36 deep here). No second episode or drain line followed on this activation in the captured window, so whether this episode cleared or the slot leaked cannot be determined from the incident evidence alone — treat as the known back-pressure condition, not a new defect.

**Impact**

Minimal for this instance: a single burst of 2 occurrences on one pod at one timestamp. The systemic impact is tracked under #1172, which shows 13M+ occurrences across ~500 pods.

**Where to look**

- `MeshWeaver.Hosting.Orleans.RoutingGrain` — dispatch-slot accounting and per-destination queue behaviour (see #1172).
- Check the episode stamp `c0d85529` in raw logs for a later/higher episode to confirm the backlog drained.

**Already known**

Almost certainly a duplicate of #1172 — same log category, same message shape, same head-of-line signature on cache/portal destinations. File for traceability, then close as a duplicate of #1172 unless the episode never drains (which would point to a leaked slot and warrant its own investigation).

---

### Evidence

| | |
|---|---|
| Fingerprint | `52e3fc831213ea4d` |
| Category | `MeshWeaver.Hosting.Orleans.RoutingGrain` |
| Severity | Critical |
| Namespace | `memex` |
| Pods | `memex-portal-deployment-5998d5fddf-9sfsv` |
| Occurrences | 2 |
| First seen | 2026-09-21 10:01:24Z |
| Last seen | 2026-09-21 10:01:24Z |
| Routing | **not determined** — no configured route matches the category `MeshWeaver.Hosting.Orleans.RoutingGrain`. This repository is the configured fallback, not a finding about who owns the fault; the category names the LOGGER, which may not be the subject. |

<details><summary>Recent log lines</summary>

```
2026-09-21 10:01:24Z memex-portal-deployment-5998d5fddf-9sfsv crit: MeshWeaver.Hosting.Orleans.RoutingGrain[0]
      [ROUTE] Routing back-pressure [c0d85529#1 started 2026-09-21T10:01:24.8564046Z]: 64 route dispatches in flight (reporting threshold 64); stream destinations queued 4, deepest per-destination queue 36, routing pool subscribing 0. Latest dispatch target portal/nodeops-9VkLPkBrRU-rwTJ4WyrfiQ — the address that happened to cross the threshold, NOT a diagnosis. A slot is held from dispatch until the leg terminates, INCLUDING the unbounded wait for a ThreadPool thread before the leg's own timeouts start, so a CPU-starved silo raises this with nothing stuck. A deepest queue of 1 or more means legs are blocked behind a leg (head-of-line on one destination); 0 means nothing is waiting on anything, so read it as load. 🚨 Deepest is sampled AT THE CROSSING, so like the in-flight count it is partly an artefact of the threshold: with N destinations sharing the backlog it is ~InFlight/N whatever is wrong. READ THE EPISODE STAMP, not the depth: a later line with a HIGHER episode on this activation means this episode drained; a line with a DIFFERENT activation id means the grain was recycled; and if neither a clear nor a higher episode ever follows, the in-flight count never fell below half the threshold — which means a leg never terminated and its slot leaked, not that the silo was busy.
2026-09-21 10:01:24Z memex-portal-deployment-5998d5fddf-9sfsv crit: MeshWeaver.Hosting.Orleans.RoutingGrain[0]
      [ROUTE] Routing back-pressure [c0d85529#1 started 2026-09-21T10:01:24.8564046Z]: 64 route dispatches in flight (reporting threshold 64); stream destinations queued 4, deepest per-destination queue 36, routing pool subscribing 0. Latest dispatch target portal/nodeops-9VkLPkBrRU-rwTJ4WyrfiQ — the address that happened to cross the threshold, NOT a diagnosis. A slot is held from dispatch until the leg terminates, INCLUDING the unbounded wait for a ThreadPool thread before the leg's own timeouts start, so a CPU-starved silo raises this with nothing stuck. A deepest queue of 1 or more means legs are blocked behind a leg (head-of-line on one destination); 0 means nothing is waiting on anything, so read it as load. 🚨 Deepest is sampled AT THE CROSSING, so like the in-flight count it is partly an artefact of the threshold: with N destinations sharing the backlog it is ~InFlight/N whatever is wrong. READ THE EPISODE STAMP, not the depth: a later line with a HIGHER episode on this activation means this episode drained; a line with a DIFFERENT activation id means the grain was recycled; and if neither a clear nor a higher episode ever follows, the in-flight count never fell below half the threshold — which means a leg never terminated and its slot leaked, not that the silo was busy.
```

</details>

<sub>Re-addressed by the current identity function: this incident inherited `e4a97855ab595beb` (Systemorph/MeshWeaver.Plugins#1796). Those nodes are superseded and will not fold, file or comment again.</sub>

items.title: [Duplicate of #17] [Epic] 개인화 GTO·Exploit 학습 시스템
items.body:
## 목적

현재의 AI 홀덤 플레이·핸드 코치·종합 리뷰 구조를, **기계적으로 검증 가능한 전략 기준선과 반복 학습 루프를 가진 개인화 훈련 시스템**으로 확장합니다.

정밀 분석 및 전체 설계 문서:

- [`docs/design/gto-learning-system-roadmap.md`](https://github.com/Sungmin-Cho/AI-Holdem/blob/docs/gto-learning-roadmap-20260831/docs/design/gto-learning-system-roadmap.md)

## 현재 코드에서 확인된 핵심 공백

- `tools/game-loop.js`의 코치는 redacted hand·기본 stats·practiceFocus를 해석하지만 GTO 빈도/EV의 권위 있는 입력이 없음
- `engine/hand.js`는 토너먼트형 blind 상승과 기본 행동 통계를 소유하므로 고정 spot 비교 환경이 없음
- `engine/views.js`에는 구조화된 결정 기록보다 LLM용 문자열 요약이 중심
- `engine/personas.js`의 성향 수치는 LLM 프롬프트 메타데이터이며 실제 장기 액션 분포를 보장하지 않음
- 이전 리뷰의 practiceFocus는 자연어 전달에는 유용하지만 영속 Skill Profile·Mistake Bank·복습 스케줄은 없음

## 설계 원칙

- 엔진은 규칙과 공개 상태의 권위만 유지
- 전략 데이터/solver가 빈도와 EV의 권위
- LLM은 검증된 결과를 설명하며 수치를 새로 만들지 않음
- `exact_ev`, `frequency_only`, `heuristic`, `unsupported`를 명시적으로 구분
- `gameEpoch + decisionId` 기반 exactly-once 집계
- 기존 Play Mode와 프로세스 안전성 불변식 유지
- 전략 데이터 source/license/version/hash 필수

## 단계

### Phase 1 — 프리플랍 Training MVP

- [ ] 고정 100BB 6-max Training Mode
- [ ] DecisionRecord/Spot schema와 preflop strategy pack
- [ ] 빈도·EV 근거 수준을 보존하는 채점기
- [ ] GTO-grounded coach와 결정 후 피드백 UI

### Phase 2 — 개인화 학습

- [ ] LearnerProfile·Leak Detector·세부 기회 통계
- [ ] Spot Drill·Mistake Bank·spaced repetition

### Phase 3 — 외부 분석/포스트플랍

- [ ] canonical hand history export와 text adapter
- [ ] 선택적 postflop solver subprocess adapter

### Phase 4 — Exploit

- [ ] Persona/StrategyPolicy 분리와 Exploit Evaluator

## 전체 완료 기준

- 사용자의 모든 평가가 어떤 provider/version/source에서 나왔는지 추적 가능
- EV가 없는 데이터에서는 EV loss를 절대 표시하지 않음
- unsupported spot에서 추정 수치를 만들지 않음
- 같은 결정이 crash/resume 후 중복 집계되지 않음
- 반복 누수가 confidence/sample과 함께 발견되고 다음 드릴 출제에 반영됨
- 게임 중 상대 비공개 정보와 실제 policy가 유출되지 않음
- 기존 `node --test` 및 프로세스/게시/재개 계약 회귀 없음

## 비고

이 Epic은 구현 순서와 공통 불변식을 관리합니다. 각 하위 이슈는 독립적인 완료 조건과 테스트 요구사항을 가집니다.

items.title: [Duplicate of #7][F01] Complete the live OpenAI-compatible tool-call round trip

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Summary

The September 12 M5 acceptance pass never verified Lumen's actual final answer or a real model-selected tool action. The current adapter can parse tool calls, but its `ChatRequest` supplies only `model`, `messages`, and `stream`; no tool definitions are advertised.

## Classification

- **QA finding:** F01; historical cases T16, T19, T38–T44.
- **Priority:** P1 acceptance gate, not a CVSS rating.
- **Evidence:** code-confirmed request omission plus a manual validation gap. A live tool-task failure was **not reproduced**.
- **Baseline:** PR #6, `7c3080ad1530fc7026b777fc211e2a68767e9e94`.

## Observed behavior and limits

Text-only runs returned IDs and `run_completed` audit events. We never retrieved their final text. A separately invoked Ollama API returned valid JSON but refused the harmless `OPENAI_COMPAT_OK` marker. `ollama ps` showed GPU residency; that cannot identify a particular Lumen run or prove its answer was correct. No live filesystem action/result/model-follow-up was captured.

Inspect `OpenAiCompatibleClient::send`, `ChatRequest`, request-message serialization, `output_from_parts`/`output_from_accumulated`, and `RunOrchestrator` message accumulation. Parsing an unsolicited call is not a complete provider tool protocol. Follow-up serialization and call IDs require verification rather than assuming every provider accepts the internal representation.

## Impact

An agent can appear healthy while doing only chat, or produce prose claiming a tool ran. Missing schemas may prevent ordinary tool selection. Lost call identity can invalidate subsequent tool results.

## Proposed implementation

1. Define provider-neutral tool descriptors and call/result IDs. Derive the offered catalog from runtime-owned registrations and current permissions; the model cannot define its own authority.
2. Serialize supported function schemas in OpenAI-compatible requests. Preserve assistant tool-call envelopes and bind each result to the corresponding call ID. Handle provider-required reasoning fields only at the adapter boundary.
3. Validate names, arguments and call multiplicity. Never concatenate unrelated streamed calls. If only one call per turn is supported, reject unsupported multiplicity explicitly instead of silently dropping it.
4. Keep all side effects on the existing normalization → capabilities/policy → approval → dispatch → audit path. Do not add an unrestricted shell or treat prose as an authorized command.
5. Add deterministic wire-level fixtures and a separately marked live Ollama smoke test using a random nonce stored only in a disposable file.
6. Capture run/provider/model identity, actual final answer and action/side-effect evidence. Missing usage stays unknown; residency is not request attribution.

## Reproduction and regression plan

These are required tests, not claims they were already executed:

- [ ] Retrieve and assert a text-only Lumen result; distinguish refusal/nonmatching content from transport failure.
- [ ] Read a nonce file through the real model. Assert exact nonce in final response and an authorized filesystem-read record.
- [ ] Ask for a small file write; assert no file before approval, then grant and verify exact bytes plus the model's returned result.
- [ ] Repeat with rejection and assert zero write effects.
- [ ] Exercise the request under a zero-grant service and assert forbidden effects never occur.
- [ ] Test unknown tool, malformed arguments, mismatched IDs, multiple/interleaved streamed calls, empty content, provider failure and cancellation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Correct outbound schemas and call/result correspondence for the supported provider.
- [ ] Live nonce read and approval-gated write have real final-answer and side-effect evidence.
- [ ] Denial/rejection cannot cause unauthorized writes.
- [ ] No success claim depends only on lifecycle events or `ollama ps`.

## Sources

- [Pinned adapter](https://github.com/black-candle-technologies/lumen/blob/7c3080ad1530fc7026b777fc211e2a68767e9e94/crates/lumen-integrations/src/openai_compatible.rs)
- [Pinned orchestrator](https://github.com/black-candle-technologies/lumen/blob/7c3080ad1530fc7026b777fc211e2a68767e9e94/crates/lumen-core/src/run.rs)
- [Ollama tool-calling protocol](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/tool-calling)
- Full historical record: `LUMEN_M5_QA_2026-09-12.md`, F01 and cases above.

## Boundaries

Fix the existing single-provider integration, not the full orchestration roadmap in #4 or compartments in #5. Work on an isolated M5 repair branch/worktree; do not touch `base/ui`, the original checkout or Riley's work. Do not merge PRs automatically or weaken any security assertion. Recheck the finding against any newer SHA before implementation.

## Parent

#809 — terminal GitHub check publication and watchdog.

Roadmap slice: #945 E4.7. Depends on trusted watchdog classification, #943 GateDecisionSummary renderer, stable coordinator authority, and hostile-head-safe posting job.

## Objective

Publish exactly one terminal GitHub check for the exact head from the verified stable result, with idempotent retries and no candidate-code execution or semantic recomputation in the publishing job.

## Scope

- Create/update one configured stable required check run keyed by repository, PR/head SHA, stable coordinator identity, and publication attempt policy.
- Map verified `ci_evidence_result` and watchdog state to GitHub terminal conclusions with explicit PASS/FAIL/NOT_PROVEN/infrastructure handling supported by the check API and branch policy.
- Render title/summary/text from the structured GateDecisionSummary, preserving exact blockers/gaps/actions/artifact refs and bounded size.
- Recheck exact PR head immediately before publication and reject stale results.
- Make retries/idempotent reruns update the intended check rather than create duplicates.
- Record check run ID, API response, exact payload digest, head SHA, stable result/watchdog refs, and publication/cleanup errors.
- Use narrow checks-write authority only in the trusted posting job; execute no candidate code.
- Keep PR inline review delivery separately transactionally receipted.

## Acceptance

- [ ] One exact-head stable result produces one terminal check.
- [ ] PASS, deterministic FAIL, and NOT_PROVEN/infrastructure states map consistently and never collapse missing evidence into success.
- [ ] Stale-head publication is rejected.
- [ ] Retry/rerun is idempotent and does not create duplicate required contexts.
- [ ] Candidate shadow output cannot alter the published result.
- [ ] Publishing job executes no candidate code/config and uses only narrow write authority.
- [ ] Payload derives from verified GateDecisionSummary and remains within GitHub limits without dropping blockers/gaps.
- [ ] Publication failure is receipted and remains distinct from code truth.

## Proof

- Fake GitHub create/update/retry/stale-head/error matrix.
- PASS/FAIL/NOT_PROVEN/watchdog-state payload goldens.
- Duplicate-context/idempotence and exact-head race fixtures.
- Permission/no-candidate-execution static tests.
- Hosted advisory/non-required publication smoke before promotion.
- Full GitHub/gate/summary/delivery/verifier/workspace/fmt/Clippy/policy.

## Non-goals

- No branch-protection mutation or sole-gate promotion.
- No code truth computation.
- No candidate shadow publication.
- No break-glass implementation.

## Rollback

Disable automated terminal publication and keep the independent deterministic baseline required. Retain stable artifacts and publication receipts; never publish from unverified candidate output.

## 목표

현재의 `플레이 → LLM 핸드 코치 → 종합 리뷰 → 다음 practiceFocus` 흐름을 다음과 같은 계량형 학습 루프로 확장합니다.

```text
DecisionContext
  → strategy evaluation
  → EV-loss grade
  → leak/skill profile
  → personalized drill
  → retest
```

LLM은 GTO 숫자나 정답을 생성하지 않고, 검증된 `DecisionGrade`를 한국어로 설명하는 계층으로 사용합니다.

## 설계 문서

- [`docs/design/GTO_LEARNING_SYSTEM_ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/Sungmin-Cho/AI-Holdem/blob/docs/gto-learning-system-roadmap-20260831/docs/design/GTO_LEARNING_SYSTEM_ROADMAP.md)

## 현재 코드에서 확인된 핵심 공백

- `engine/views.js::turnSummary()`가 기계 상태를 한국어 문자열로 만들고 `tools/game-loop.js::legalFromMessage()`가 이를 다시 정규식으로 파싱함
- 코치가 redacted hand/stats/practiceFocus만 보고 평가하며 strategy distribution·action EV·provenance가 없음

- `engine/personas.js`의 bluff/3-bet 성향은 LLM 힌트이며 실제 policy 빈도를 보장하지 않음
- 자연어 practiceFocus는 존재하지만 영속 Skill Profile, Mistake Bank, 복습 scheduler가 없음

## 세부 이슈

- [ ] GTO-01 — 구조화된 DecisionContext와 canonical position
- [ ] GTO-02 — tournament/cash/drill 모드와 fixed-blind 6-max
- [ ] GTO-03 — preflop strategy store와 EV-loss grader
- [ ] GTO-04 — grounded coach와 사후 feedback UI

## 단계

1. Contract foundation: GTO-01
2. Preflop fundamentals: GTO-02, GTO-03, GTO-04
3. Adaptive learning: GTO-05, GTO-06
4. Deterministic exploit training: GTO-07, GTO-08

## 제품 성공 지표

- supported decision coverage

- repeat mistake rate
- 1/3/7/14일 복습 유지율

## 비범위

items.title: [Duplicate of #24] [Opponent] LLM 페르소나와 deterministic Strategy Policy를 분리한다
items.body:
## 배경

현재 `engine/personas.js`는 TAG/LAG/Nit/CallingStation/Maniac/Trickster를 만들고 다음 값을 `tools/player-prompt.md`에 전달합니다.

- `bluffFreq`
- `threeBetFreq`
- `tiltProne`
- personality/speech

그러나 이 값은 LLM에게 주는 성향 힌트입니다. 예를 들어 `threeBetFreq: 0.30`이 실제 가능한 3-bet spot에서 장기적으로 30%에 수렴하거나, Calling Station이 정의된 정도만큼 fold를 줄인다고 기계적으로 보장하지 않습니다. `Math.random()` 기반 tilt 결정도 seed로 재현되지 않습니다.

실력 훈련과 exploit 평가는 **상대 정책을 알고 재현할 수 있어야** 하므로, 캐릭터 표현과 액션 선택을 분리해야 합니다.

## 선행 조건

- #19 DecisionContext
- #20 preflop reference strategy

## 목표

두 실행 모드를 명시적으로 지원합니다.

### Play Mode

- 기존 LLM player decision 유지
- 이름/말투/성격 중심의 자유로운 persona 경험 보존

### Training/Policy Mode

- strategy policy가 action mix와 실제 action을 결정
- LLM은 선택적으로 narration/persona 표현만 담당
- 동일 seed + 동일 context에서 동일 action 재현
- 실제 policy/archetype은 종합 리뷰 전 사용자에게 숨김

## 모델 분리

```json
{
  "playerId": "p1",
  "persona": {
    "name": "김민준",
    "speech": "...",
    "personality": "..."
  },
  "policy": {
    "policyId": "calling-station-v1",
    "archetype": "CallingStation",
    "version": 1,
    "seed": "..."
  }
}
```

`persona`는 표현 계층이고, `policy`가 전략 계층입니다.

## Policy 인터페이스

```js
policy.evaluate(decisionContext) => {
  status: 'evaluated' | 'unsupported',
  mix: {
    fold: 0.20,
    call: 0.70,
    raise: 0.10
  },
  source: {
    baselineStrategyId: '...',
    transformId: 'calling-station-v1'
  }
}

policy.sample(mix, seededRng) => chosenAction
```

- legal action 밖의 확률은 0
- 남은 확률은 정규화
- 합이 1이 아니면 fail-closed
- unsupported일 때의 fallback 정책을 명시
- 임의 LLM 판단으로 policy 결과를 바꾸지 않음

## 초기 policy transform

정확한 수치는 테스트 fixture/config로 정의하고 한 파일에서 버전 관리합니다.

- `baseline-v1`: reference strategy mix 그대로
- `tag-v1`: marginal continue 감소, value aggression 유지
- `lag-v1`: open/3-bet 후보 확장
- `nit-v1`: continue/defend 감소, overfold 증가
- `calling-station-v1`: fold 감소, call 증가, bluff aggression 감소
- `maniac-v1`: legal raise 쪽으로 확률 이동
- `trickster-v1`: baseline의 mixed action을 확대하되 seed 재현

변환은 action 의미와 spot family를 알아야 하며, 단순히 모든 상황에서 `raise += 0.2`처럼 적용하지 않습니다.

## 재현성

- game/session seed를 persisted config에 저장
- persona 생성, policy 선택, action sampling이 모두 동일 RNG abstraction 사용
- `Math.random()` 직접 호출 금지
- resume 이후 RNG progression 또는 decision-specific derived seed가 동일해야 함

권장 방식은 `sessionSeed + playerId + decisionId + policyVersion` 해시에서 decision RNG를 파생해, 중간 프로세스 재시작과 호출 순서 차이에 영향을 받지 않게 하는 것입니다.

## 정보 공개 경계

- 게임 중 UI/turn summary에는 `policyId`, archetype transform, 실제 fold/raise bias를 공개하지 않음
- `players.json`은 내부 파일이므로 coach/evaluator redaction deny list를 유지
- 종합 리뷰에서만 actual persona/policy와 사용자의 읽기 결과를 공개

## 관련 파일

### 수정

- `engine/personas.js`
  - persona metadata와 policy descriptor 분리
  - 직접 `Math.random()` 제거
- `engine/hand.js`
  - session seed/config 보존이 필요한 경우 추가
- `engine/views.js`
  - public view에서 policy private field 제외
- `tools/game-loop.js`
  - `decideWithWatchdog()` 경로와 policy decision 경로 분기
  - policy player는 LLM warmup/session을 만들지 않음
  - metrics에 `decisionSource: llm|policy` 추가
- `tools/player-prompt.md`
  - Play Mode persona 전용임을 명확화
- `tools/player-runtime.js`
  - policy 좌석에 불필요한 runtime session 생성 방지
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `README.md`

### 신규

- `strategy/opponents/schema.js`
- `strategy/opponents/policy-registry.js`
- `strategy/opponents/policy-transform.js`
- `strategy/opponents/sample-action.js`
- `strategy/opponents/policies/*.json`
- `engine/rng.js` 또는 공용 deterministic RNG 모듈

### 신규 테스트 후보

- `test/opponent-policy.test.js`
- `test/policy-sampling.test.js`
- `test/persona-policy-privacy.test.js`
- `test/policy-resume-determinism.test.js`

### 회귀 테스트

- `test/player-runtime.test.js`
- `test/game-loop.test.js`
- 기존 persona/view/redaction 테스트

## 완료 조건

- [ ] persona metadata와 action policy가 서로 다른 schema/모듈에 존재한다.
- [ ] Play Mode의 기존 LLM decision 경로가 유지된다.
- [ ] Training Mode에서는 policy가 action의 유일한 정본이다.
- [ ] 동일 session seed/context/policy version에서 동일 action이 재현된다.
- [ ] resume 전후 동일 decision의 결과가 달라지지 않는다.
- [ ] policy mix는 legal action만 포함하고 합이 1이다.
- [ ] 각 archetype transform이 fixture에서 의도한 방향으로 baseline을 변경한다.
- [ ] aggregate simulation test가 seed 기반으로 안정적이며 flaky하지 않다.
- [ ] policy가 지원하지 않는 spot의 fallback이 명시적이다.
- [ ] 게임 중 사용자에게 policyId/archetype/private frequency가 노출되지 않는다.
- [ ] 종합 리뷰에는 실제 policy와 사용자의 대응 평가가 분리되어 표시된다.
- [ ] policy player 때문에 LLM runtime probe/warmup 비용이 발생하지 않는다.

## 범위 밖

- exploit best-response 계산
- postflop solver-based policy
- self-play reinforcement learning

Roadmap: #17

items.title: [Duplicate of #19] [Learning] 학습 계층과 DecisionSnapshot/StrategyEvaluation 계약을 추가한다
items.body:
## 배경

현재 엔진은 규칙과 상태 전이를, sidecar는 LLM/게시/종료를 잘 분리하고 있습니다. 그러나 사용자 선택을 GTO 기준과 비교하려면 핸드 기록의 여러 필드를 사후 재구성해야 하며, 평가 결과의 공용 계약도 없습니다.

`tools/game-loop.js`에 spot 판정과 평가 로직을 직접 추가하면 이미 큰 sidecar의 책임이 더 커집니다. 먼저 순수 `learning/` 계층과 두 핵심 계약을 고정해야 합니다.

설계 문서: `docs/design/gto-learning-system-roadmap.md` (`docs/gto-learning-roadmap-20260831` 브랜치)

## 목표

1. 엔진이 의사결정 시점의 canonical facts를 `DecisionSnapshot`으로 제공한다.
2. 전략 provider의 결과를 `StrategyEvaluation`으로 표준화한다.
3. `learning/`은 엔진 상태를 변경하지 않고 네트워크·LLM·child process를 호출하지 않는 순수 계층으로 둔다.
4. unsupported/unmatched/EV 미지원 상태를 명시적으로 표현한다.

## 제안 계약

### DecisionSnapshot 최소 필드

- schemaVersion, gameEpoch, handNo, decisionId, actorId
- mode, tableSize, street, position, buttonPlayerId
- blind/ante, holeCards, board
- potBefore, stackBefore, effectiveStack, currentBet, toCall
- publicActions
- legal(canCheck/callAmount/canRaise/minRaiseTo/maxRaiseTo)
- chosenAction

### StrategyEvaluation 최소 필드

- schemaVersion
- provider id/version/abstraction
- normalized spotId
- match status: `matched | unsupported | ambiguous`
- size mapping과 limitations
- action별 frequency와 optional evBB
- chosenKey, bestKey
- optional evLossBB
- grade: `correct | inaccuracy | mistake | blunder | ungraded`

## 변경 후보

- `ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `engine/views.js` 또는 새 `engine/decision-trace.js`
- `learning/contracts.js`
- `learning/canonical-json.js`
- `learning/grade-policy.js`
- `test/decision-snapshot.test.js`
- `test/learning-contracts.test.js`

포지션 계산은 현재 `engine/views.js`의 `positionsOf`와 별도 구현하지 말고 canonical helper로 공용화합니다.

## 완료 조건

- [ ] 모든 사용자 action에 정확히 하나의 snapshot을 연결할 수 있다.
- [ ] snapshot은 한 `stateVersion`의 facts와 `legalFor` 결과에 대응한다.
- [ ] snapshot/evaluation은 schema version과 validator를 갖는다.
- [ ] unknown schema와 malformed input은 fail-closed한다.
- [ ] frequency-only provider에서 `evLossBB`는 `null`이며 임의 EV를 만들지 않는다.
- [ ] unsupported multiway/stack/sizing은 `ungraded`로 보존된다.
- [ ] canonical serialization과 digest가 재실행·resume 뒤에도 동일하다.
- [ ] `learning/`이 engine state, network, LLM, child process에 의존하지 않는다.
- [ ] `ARCHITECTURE.md`에 새 계층과 의존 방향이 문서화된다.
- [ ] 기존 `node --test`가 통과한다.

## 필수 테스트

- snapshot legal 수치와 `legalFor` 일치
- raise amount가 기존 계약대로 raise-to임을 검증
- heads-up/6-max position 매핑
- malformed/unknown schema 거부
- unsupported evaluation에서 추천/EV 미생성
- 같은 입력의 digest deterministic 보장

## 범위 밖

- 실제 GTO 전략 데이터 번들
- postflop solver 연동
- UI 구현
- 장기 skill profile

items.title: Portal boot fails when the PostgreSQL host does not resolve (memex) — duplicate of #3780
items.body:
**Duplicate of [Systemorph/MeshWeaver#3780](https://github.com/Systemorph/MeshWeaver/issues/3780)** — the same boot failure at a second log site. #3780 was filed from the silo-lifecycle fingerprint ([Admin/_LogIncident/0b1877ae6c51353f](@/Admin/_LogIncident/0b1877ae6c51353f)) and is the *inner* failure: the Orleans `MembershipTableManager` aborting silo start at stage `RuntimeGrainServices`. This entry is the *outer* aggregate of the same boot — the .NET generic host giving up, with the portal's startup wrapper (`RunOrExitOnCancelledStartup`) observing the failed start and exiting the container. Close as a duplicate of #3780; this ticket exists so the second log site is traceable and links back.

## What is failing

During the record-driven reconcile roll of the `memex` control instance (helm `--wait` upgrade launched about a minute before the failure), the roll's fresh surge pod failed to boot: the first PostgreSQL connection attempt could not resolve the database hostname — DNS resolution failed (`Name or service not known` out of `Dns.GetHostEntryOrAddressesCore`) before any TCP dial was attempted. The pod then cycled through repeated failed boots (the recurrence is carried on the sibling fingerprint above).

## Probable cause — medium confidence

DNS resolution of the PostgreSQL host fails inside the boot window. This fingerprint adds no evidence beyond #3780, which names the two candidates and the one-command discriminator (`getent hosts <db-host>` from the pod): either a transient resolver/CoreDNS blip, or a wrong/default-derived connection-string value on this pod. The second is live here because the pod was created by a re-apply of the instance record moments earlier, and the connection strings reach the pod only through `memex-portal-secrets` (rendered from the Key Vault values half no repository holds) and `memex-kv-secrets` — no committed file states the host. Host resolves now → resolver blip; does not → bad rendered value.

## Impact

A delayed roll, not an outage: the failing pod is one of two replicas, and the rollout is surge-first (`maxUnavailable: 0`), so the previously ready pods kept serving while the new pod cycled — the reconcile was still inside its helm `--wait` window when this incident fired. The exposure is that `memex` is the **control instance** (infrastructure control, accounting, home of the Deployments records): a persistent version of this failure stalls every roll of it, in the same "safe but stuck" shape as a gate-held rollout.

## Where to look

- [Systemorph/MeshWeaver#3780](https://github.com/Systemorph/MeshWeaver/issues/3780) — the canonical ticket for this boot: same pod, same second, full diagnosis path and discriminator.
- `Memex.Portal.Shared.CancelledStartup.RunOrExitOnCancelledStartup` (Systemorph/Memex) — the startup wrapper that observes and rethrows the failed host start; the top application frame of this fingerprint.
- [Deployments/memex](@/Deployments/memex) — the instance record; `ConnectionStrings__memex` arrives via `memex-kv-secrets`, and both `ConnectionStrings__memex` and `ConnectionStrings__orleans` via `vaultValuesKeys` on `memex-portal-secrets` (rendered from `helm-values-memex`, held in no repository).
- [Deployments/memex-reconcile-20260909-final](@/Deployments/memex-reconcile-20260909-final) — the reconcile that created the failing pod; its `helm upgrade --atomic --wait` was still waiting when this incident fired.

items.body: ### Description After updating Elementor Core to version 4.3.0, the following PHP warning appears both on the frontend and inside the Elementor editor: Warning: Attempt to read property "ID" on null in /wp-content/plugins/elementor/core/base/document.php on line 356 The warning is triggered when a previously saved Elementor header template is imported into a new header document. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new header in Elementor Theme Builder. 2. Open the new header with Elementor. 3. Confirm that no PHP warning is displayed. 4. Import a previously saved header template. 5. The warning appears twice above the header. 6. Removing the imported block does not immediately remove the warnings. 7. Roll back Elementor Core from 4.3.0 to 4.2.3. 8. The warning disappears completely. The affected line in core/base/document.php is: $post_id = $this->post->ID; It appears that $this->post can be null after importing or rendering a saved header template, but get_main_id() does not validate it before accessing ID. ### Expected behavior Saved header templates should be imported and rendered without PHP warnings, and get_main_id() should safely handle a missing post object. Actual behavior: Elementor attempts to read the ID property from a null post object. The problem is reproducible in Elementor 4.3.0 and disappears after rolling back to Elementor 4.2.3. ### Elementor System Info ```txt == Server Environment == Operating System: Linux Software: items.title: [DUPLICATE of #44] [P1-06] Repair the matcher and URL-extractor document pipeline
items.body:
## Confirmed defects
`source/actor-systems/matcher-actor.lisp` defines patterns and a URL extractor, but no actor consumes incoming documents and evaluates `*document-patterns*`. The registered pattern is therefore dead.

Additional defects:
- The URL extractor publishes generated relations/URLs directly to `documents.new.*`, bypassing validation, persistence, idempotency, and the canonical ingest flow.
- `as-json` returns a JSOWN object while publication expects normalized serialized JSON; behavior depends on a compatibility conversion.
- The URL regular expression is malformed/fragile and has no corpus tests.
- Pattern subscriptions store raw actor references/names without lifecycle handling.
- Pattern registration is global mutable state and cannot be isolated per runtime/dataset.
- Errors in one pattern can block or discard all pattern work.

## Required changes
- Implement a typed document-pattern ingress component/router pool.
- Bind it declaratively through actor/dataset manifests to selected `documents.new.<dtype>` flows.
- Validate accepted dtypes and schema versions.
- Route generated documents through canonical ingest, never directly through `documents.new`.
- Make pattern registry runtime-scoped and lifecycle-aware.
- Add per-pattern deadlines, bounded output count, failure isolation, provenance, and metrics.
- Replace the regex with a tested URI extraction strategy and normalization step.

## Acceptance tests
- A message fixture containing URLs produces persisted canonical URL and relation documents with provenance.
- Duplicate URLs are handled according to idempotency policy.
- One failing pattern does not prevent other patterns from running.
- Output limits prevent a single document from generating unbounded work.
- Stopped/restarted subscribers are resolved through current component handles.

## Objective

```text
T1 early specialist completes
T2 semantic proof intent admitted
T3 canonical task starts
T4 slowest primary specialist remains active
T5 receipt changes the exact claim
T6 final ReviewJudgment compiles
T7 delivery is confirmed or explicitly unnecessary
T8 FinalizedOutcome is emitted with zero pending runnable work
```

Required ordering:

```text
T1 < T2 <= T3 < T4
T5 < T6 < T8
```

## Scope

- Build one frozen production-style fixture with a materially relevant early proof question and a deliberately delayed specialist.
- Exercise RepositoryContract, MaterialChangeMap, Required spine, portfolio, SharedRunPlan, TaskLedger/scheduler, Cargo/cache resource, model stream, exact claim effect, final lead, transactional delivery, gate summary, and finalized outcome.

- Mark mechanically mandatory, optional, irrelevant, unsupported, and manually requested programmes explicitly.
- Start from deterministic facts; model inference cannot add canonical material edges.
- Suppress programmes whose question is already answered by current receipts/thread state where policy allows.
- Record selection reasons, supporting material-map edges, and expected proof-intent families.
- Emit a shadow programme plan and verifier.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Workflow-only, tests-only, parser, unsafe/native, schema/verifier and docs changes receive materially different candidate sets.
- [ ] Irrelevant Bun/native programmes are absent on ordinary Rust tooling changes.
- [ ] Every selected programme has one distinct question and exact material evidence.
- [ ] A mechanically mandatory trust/lifetime programme cannot be omitted by optional routing.
- [ ] Already answered questions may be suppressed only with current-revision/thread evidence.
- [ ] Unknown material gaps remain explicit.
- [ ] Candidate generation is deterministic and provider-independent.

## Proof

- Diff-class/material-map goldens across representative surfaces.
- Irrelevant-programme and mandatory-programme negatives.
- Already-answered current-receipt/thread fixture.
- Stable-order and forged-material-edge verifier tests.
- Full contract/impact/model-plan/workspace/fmt/Clippy/policy.

## Non-goals

- No LLM router or model selection; sibling B5.3.
- No model call launch.
- No final ReviewJudgment.
- No historical programme ranking.

## Rollback

Keep deterministic candidates in shadow while retaining current lane defaults.

labels.name: epic
labels.description: Multi-milestone epic tracking a product initiative

items.body:
## Parent

#928 — required-first evidence portfolio.

Roadmap slice: #945 B4.1. Depends on #958 pure outcome semantics and #941 spine contract types where available.

## Objective

Land the pure policy model distinguishing evidence that must exist for PASS from dynamically selected detective proof and review-only advisory evidence.

## Contract

```text
Required
  absent/unavailable -> NOT_PROVEN
  deterministic violation -> FAIL
  satisfying current receipt -> satisfied

Detective
  unselected/deferred -> nonblocking
  executed deterministic result -> may affect gate under explicit repo policy

Advisory
  review evidence only
```

## Scope

- Define typed consumer requirement and gate-effect policy values.
- Define deterministic result-to-outcome truth tables independent of source/selector/model.
- Preserve multiple consumer classes on one execution.
- Distinguish selection/defer state from execution terminal result.
- Bind semantics to current RevisionIdentity and accepted receipt class.
- Keep model judgment outside deterministic result authority.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Missing Required evidence prevents PASS.
- [ ] Unselected Detective work does not make Required evidence incomplete.
- [ ] An executed approved Detective test may deterministically fail under explicit policy without model verdict authority.
- [ ] Advisory results never directly alter CI evidence truth.
- [ ] One task may satisfy consumers with different classes without collapsing their semantics.
- [ ] Infrastructure unavailability remains distinct from code failure.
- [ ] Pure truth table is order-independent and model-off compatible.

## Proof

- Complete class × selected/deferred × terminal-result matrix.
- Multi-consumer same-task fixture.
- Model-discovery/no-model-authority negative.
- Missing/stale/wrong receipt cases.
- Serialization/version tests plus fmt/check/Clippy/policy.

## Non-goals

- No candidate normalization; sibling B4.2.
- No ranking/admission.
- No live gate switch.
- No model prompt change.

## Rollback

Remove unused pure policy types without changing current planners or gate behavior.

## Source boundary

This slice covers the opening definition of the p-adic integer ring, ending before §1.2 Proposition 1.

For a prime `p` and `n ≥ 1`, set `A_n = Z / p^n Z`; use the canonical surjections `A_n → A_{n-1}` to form the inverse system; define `Z_p` as its projective/inverse limit; expose elements as compatible sequences and ring operations componentwise. No book prose/image should be committed.

General category/inverse-limit, quotient-ring, finite-product, topology, and compactness infrastructure is allowed.

For each enabled calendar, reminder, notification, location, storage or accessibility adapter:

items.body:
## 배경

`engine/personas.js`는 TAG/LAG/Nit/CallingStation/Maniac/Trickster archetype과 bluff/3-bet/tilt 성향을 만들고, `tools/player-prompt.md`가 이를 LLM에 전달합니다. 하지만 이 수치는 행동 정책의 장기 빈도를 보장하지 않으므로 exploit 훈련의 재현 가능한 상대 모델로 사용할 수 없습니다.

선행 이슈: GTO-01, GTO-03

설계 문서: [`GTO_LEARNING_SYSTEM_ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/Sungmin-Cho/AI-Holdem/blob/docs/gto-learning-system-roadmap-20260831/docs/design/GTO_LEARNING_SYSTEM_ROADMAP.md)

## 목표

```text
Persona Layer
  name / speech / personality

Strategy Policy Layer
  baseline / deviations / sampler / provenance
```

## controller 모드

- `llm`: 현재 플레이 방식 유지
- `policy`: 순수 policy engine이 action 선택
- `hybrid`: policy가 action을 결정하고 LLM은 말투·내러티브만 생성

## 권장 신규 모듈

```text
opponents/
  policy-schema.js
  policy-engine.js
  policy-sampler.js
  policies/
```

## 정책 요구사항

- policyId/schemaVersion/provenance
- baseline strategy capability
- spot tag별 action frequency delta 또는 명시 distribution
- legal action renormalization
- seeded reproducibility
- unsupported spot fallback 정책 명시
- 실제 session empirical frequency 기록

## 대상 파일

- `engine/personas.js`
- `tools/player-prompt.md`
- `tools/player-runtime.js`
- `tools/game-loop.js`
- 신규 `opponents/*`
- player/session persistence
- UI archetype 공개/리뷰

## 완료 조건

- [ ] 기존 `llm` mode의 플레이가 호환됨
- [ ] 동일 seed/policy/context에서 동일 action sequence를 재현함
- [ ] Calling Station/Nit/LAG의 핵심 deviation이 unit fixture로 검증됨
- [ ] illegal action 제거 후 distribution이 안전하게 재정규화됨
- [ ] policy action은 LLM 응답 실패와 무관하게 결정 가능함
- [ ] hybrid mode에서 LLM이 policy action을 변경하지 못함
- [ ] empirical action frequency와 target frequency를 비교할 수 있음
- [ ] policy provenance가 final review에 연결됨
- [ ] 상대 비공개 policy 정보는 게임 종료 전 사용자에게 노출되지 않음

## 비범위

- nodelock solver
- LLM table talk의 고도화

items.title: [Duplicate of #24] [Phase 4] Persona와 StrategyPolicy 분리 및 Exploit Evaluator
items.body:
## 배경

현재 `engine/personas.js`는 TAG/LAG/Nit/CallingStation/Maniac/Trickster에 말투·성격·블러프 빈도·3-bet 성향·tilt 여부를 부여하고, `tools/player-prompt.md`를 통해 LLM 플레이어 행동을 유도합니다.

이는 캐릭터성과 변동성에는 좋지만 다음을 보장하지 않습니다.

- 설정한 3-bet/블러프 빈도가 실제 표본에서 수렴하는가
- 특정 node에서 baseline 대비 어떤 deviation을 갖는가
- 사용자가 그 deviation을 올바르게 exploit했는가
- 같은 seed에서 동일한 상대 행동을 재현할 수 있는가

전체 설계:

- [`docs/design/gto-learning-system-roadmap.md`](https://github.com/Sungmin-Cho/AI-Holdem/blob/docs/gto-learning-roadmap-20260831/docs/design/gto-learning-system-roadmap.md)

## 목표

- 표현 계층 `Persona`와 행동 권위 `StrategyPolicy` 분리
- baseline 전략에 대한 node별 deviation 모델
- seed 기반 stochastic sampling
- 게임 종료 후 GTO score와 exploit score 분리
- 상대 읽기 정확도 평가

## 제안 구조

```text
Opponent
 ├─ Persona
 │   ├─ name
 │   ├─ speech
 │   └─ personality
 └─ StrategyPolicy
     ├─ baselineProvider
     ├─ deviations
     ├─ samplingSeed
     └─ disclosurePolicy
```

## Policy 예시

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "id": "calling-station-v1",
  "baseline": "nlhe-6max-100bb-v1",
  "deviations": [
    {
      "spotFamily": "river.facing_bet",
      "action": "call",
      "mode": "add_probability",
      "value": 0.2
    }
  ],
  "seed": "...",
  "disclose": "after_session"
}
```

실제 구현에서는 frequency normalization과 legal-action clamp 규칙을 명시해야 합니다.

## 실행 모드

- Play Mode: 현재 LLM player 유지 가능
- Exploit Mode: policy runtime이 액션 권위
- LLM은 선택적으로 액션 후 캐릭터 문구만 생성
- LLM이 policy가 선택한 액션을 변경하지 못함

## 평가 분리

### GTO score

baseline provider 대비 사용자의 의사결정 품질

### Exploit score

실제 상대 policy에 대해 더 높은 EV를 만드는 대응 여부

예:

```text
GTO 기준: river bluff 빈도 정상
Exploit 기준: 과도하게 콜하는 상대에게 bluff 과다
```

두 점수를 하나로 합쳐 원인을 숨기지 않습니다.

## 상대 읽기 평가

게임 중 사용자가 상대를 TAG/Nit/CallingStation 등으로 추정하거나 행동 특성을 선택적으로 기록할 수 있게 하고, 종료 후 실제 policy와 비교합니다.

실제 policy와 private deviation은 세션 종료 전 UI·코치·LLM prompt에 노출하지 않습니다.

## 완료 조건

- [ ] Persona와 StrategyPolicy의 타입·저장·표시 책임 분리
- [ ] Exploit Mode에서 policy가 유일한 액션 권위
- [ ] seed 고정 시 동일 action sequence 재현
- [ ] 대규모 simulation에서 설정 frequency가 허용 오차 내 수렴
- [ ] legal action에 맞게 distribution normalize
- [ ] unsupported baseline node의 fallback 정책 명시
- [ ] 실제 policy/deviation이 게임 중 공개 payload에 없음
- [ ] per-hand coach가 hidden policy를 추측하거나 전달하지 않음
- [ ] 종료 후에만 실제 policy와 읽기 평가 공개
- [ ] GTO score와 exploit score 별도 계산·표시
- [ ] LLM narration 실패가 policy 액션에 영향 없음
- [ ] `node --test` 통과

## 테스트 요구사항

- deterministic seed
- frequency convergence
- legal-action clamp
- zero/negative/overflow probability validation
- hidden policy leak denylist
- LLM action override 시도
- policy unavailable fallback
- baseline unsupported node
- Calling Station/Nit/LAG 대표 deviation
- GTO good / exploit bad 사례
- GTO bad / exploit good 사례

## 비목표

- 초기 버전에서 완전한 opponent modeling ML 구현
- policy가 없는 임의 LLM 행동을 사후에 exact exploit EV로 평가
- 게임 중 상대의 실제 아키타입 공개

## 선행

- Strategy provider/grade 계약
- seed 가능한 Training Mode
- LearnerProfile
- postflop exploit EV를 위해서는 Postflop solver provider 필요

items.title: [Duplicate of #27] [Interop] Canonical Hand History와 PokerStars-style exporter를 추가한다
items.body:
## 배경

현재 engine hand archive에는 export에 필요한 정보가 대부분 존재합니다.

- hand number, level, blinds, button
- seat/start stack/end stack
- hole cards
- street별 board
- action sequence
- folded/all-in
- pots, winners, showdown reveals/mucks
- uncalled bet 반환 정보가 engine event/record에 존재

하지만 외부 분석기나 별도 연구 도구가 읽을 수 있는 표준 텍스트 Hand History exporter는 없습니다.

직접 특정 analyzer 내부 포맷에 결합하기보다, 먼저 **AI-Holdem canonical HH 모델**을 만들고 그 위에 format adapter를 둡니다.

## 목표

1. archive record를 검증된 canonical hand-history 객체로 변환
2. PokerStars-style 텍스트 export adapter 제공
3. session/단일 hand export CLI
4. 미공개 상대 hole cards를 절대 export하지 않음
5. golden fixture와 round-trip invariant로 포맷 회귀 방지

## Canonical HH 예시

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "sessionId": "...",
  "handNo": 12,
  "mode": "training",
  "tableFormat": "6max",
  "currency": "CHIP",
  "buttonSeat": 3,
  "blinds": { "sb": 25, "bb": 50 },
  "seats": [
    { "seat": 1, "playerId": "user", "name": "Hero", "startStack": 5000 }
  ],
  "hero": {
    "playerId": "user",
    "cards": ["As", "Jh"]
  },
  "streets": {
    "preflop": { "actions": [] },
    "flop": { "board": ["..."], "actions": [] },
    "turn": { "board": ["..."], "actions": [] },
    "river": { "board": ["..."], "actions": [] }
  },
  "summary": {
    "pots": [],
    "reveals": [],
    "mucks": [],
    "endStacks": {}
  }
}
```

## Privacy 변환

내부 full record에 모든 dealt hole cards가 있더라도 canonical/export 결과는 다음만 포함합니다.

- Hero에게 실제로 배분된 카드
- showdown에서 공개된 opponent cards
- 공개되지 않은 opponent cards는 생략
- muck player에 대해 내부 카드 값을 텍스트에 쓰지 않음

이 규칙은 `redactRecord()`와 별도 구현으로 중복하지 말고, 공통 visibility helper 또는 fixture로 정합성을 검증합니다.

## Action 의미 정규화

현재 action의 `amount`는 action 종류에 따라 의미가 다를 수 있으므로 exporter 전에 canonical 필드를 명확히 합니다.

```json
{
  "action": "raise",
  "putIn": 100,
  "raiseTo": 250,
  "callAmountBefore": 50,
  "allIn": false
}
```

- `call`: 이번 action에서 실제 투입한 칩
- `raise`: `raiseTo`와 실제 추가 투입량을 모두 보존
- short all-in, uncalled bet, side pot을 정확히 재구성
- exporter가 UI용 문장을 역파싱하지 않음

## Timestamp gap

engine은 wall clock을 몰라야 하므로 hand timestamp를 엔진 로직에 직접 넣지 않습니다.

제안:

- sidecar/archive manifest가 `startedAt`, `finishedAt`을 hand metadata로 저장
- 과거 archive에 timestamp가 없으면 exporter가 export time을 실제 hand time처럼 가장하지 않음
- 포맷상 값이 필수이면 `unknown` 정책 또는 session 시작 시각+명시적 synthetic flag 사용

## CLI

```bash
# 현재/아카이브 세션 전체
node tools/export-hand-history.js \
  --game-dir game \
  --format pokerstars \
  --out exports/session-<id>.txt

# 한 핸드
node tools/export-hand-history.js \
  --hand game/hands/hand-0012.json \
  --format canonical-json \
  --out exports/hand-0012.json
```

출력 경로는 사용자가 지정하고, 기본적으로 기존 archive를 변경하지 않습니다.

## 외부 analyzer 호환성

- 첫 목표는 문법적으로 일관된 PokerStars-style subset입니다.
- 특정 외부 서비스 호환을 완료 조건으로 주장하려면 실제 업로드 fixture와 서비스명/검증일을 문서화합니다.
- analyzer가 지원하지 않는 multiway/size/stack spot은 exporter 성공과 전략 분석 성공을 구분합니다.

## 관련 파일

### 수정

- `engine/hand.js`
  - canonical export에 필요한 action 의미가 누락된 경우 record 보강
- `engine/views.js`
  - visibility/redaction helper 재사용 가능성 정리
- `engine/game-archive.js`
  - archive manifest/timestamp metadata
- `engine/cli.js`
  - 필요 시 read-only hand/session listing command
- `tools/game-loop.js`
  - hand started/finished metadata 기록
- `.gitignore`
  - `exports/`
- `README.md`
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`

### 신규

- `interop/hand-history/schema.js`
- `interop/hand-history/from-engine-record.js`
- `interop/hand-history/privacy.js`
- `interop/hand-history/pokerstars.js`
- `interop/hand-history/canonical-json.js`
- `tools/export-hand-history.js`
- `exports/.gitkeep` 또는 실행 시 생성

### 신규 테스트 후보

- `test/hand-history-canonical.test.js`
- `test/hand-history-privacy.test.js`
- `test/hand-history-pokerstars.test.js`
- `test/fixtures/hand-history/*.json`
- `test/fixtures/hand-history/*.txt`

## 필수 fixture

- [ ] heads-up fold preflop
- [ ] 6-max single-raised pot
- [ ] 3-bet/4-bet
- [ ] short-stack all-in
- [ ] multiway all-in + side pots
- [ ] split pot + odd chip
- [ ] uncalled bet return
- [ ] showdown reveal/muck 혼합
- [ ] hero bust
- [ ] Training Mode stack reset이 hand pot에 섞이지 않는 사례

## 완료 조건

- [ ] canonical HH schema가 versioned이고 validate 가능하다.
- [ ] 같은 archive는 byte-stable한 export를 만든다(허용된 timestamp 제외 정책 포함).
- [ ] raise-to/put-in/call amount 의미가 명확하다.
- [ ] side pot, odd chip, uncalled return, all-in을 fixture와 일치하게 출력한다.
- [ ] Hero cards와 공개 showdown cards 외 opponent hole cards가 출력되지 않는다.
- [ ] muck된 카드가 내부 full record에 있어도 export에 나타나지 않는다.
- [ ] 과거 archive의 누락 필드는 명시적 warning/unsupported로 처리한다.
- [ ] session export가 hand number 순서를 안정적으로 유지한다.
- [ ] 특정 analyzer 호환 주장은 실제 검증 fixture가 있을 때만 문서화한다.
- [ ] exporter는 engine state/archive를 수정하지 않는다.

## 범위 밖

- 외부 서비스 자동 업로드/인증
- proprietary hand-history parser 복제
- solver 호출

Roadmap: #17
