items.title: yam produces invalid YAML for alias mapping values, and drops anchors on mappings/sequences
items.body:
## Summary

Formatting a document that uses YAML anchors and aliases produces output that
no longer parses. There are three related defects in
`pkg/yam/formatted/encoder.go`:

1. **An alias used as a mapping value goes on its own line** at the key's
   indentation instead of after the colon. The result is invalid YAML.
2. **Anchors on mapping and sequence values are dropped** (`base: &base` →
   `base:`). Even with (1) fixed, the output would still fail because the
   aliases would refer to an undefined anchor.
3. **Merge keys get an explicit tag** (`<<:` → `!!merge <<:`). It's still
   valid YAML, but it's noisy.

The two that break output, (1) and (2), hit any config that uses anchors to
share values, such as docker-compose `x-` blocks and CI configs that use
`<<: *defaults`. Running `yam` over those files corrupts them.

## Why this hasn't come up before

yam is mostly run on Chainguard melange configs, and those don't use anchors
or aliases. I parsed every `.yaml` file under the package and pipeline
directories of chainguard-dev/stereo (141863b5e9c, 2026-10-01) with PyYAML and
counted anchor and alias events. None had any:

| stereo directory (recursive) | YAML files | using anchors/aliases |
|---|---|---|
| `os/` | 3789 | 0 |
| `enterprise-packages/` | 6153 | 0 |
| `extra-packages/` | 694 | 0 |
| `pipelines/` | 129 | 0 |

So melange users are unlikely to be affected today. Anyone running yam on
other YAML (compose files, CI configs, Kubernetes manifests), or on a future
melange config that uses anchors, would get broken output.

## Reproduction

On `main` (8b0731e):

```console
$ cat t.yaml
base: &base
  x: 1
derived:
  <<: *base
  y: 2
ref: *base
$ yam t.yaml && cat t.yaml
base:
  x: 1
derived:
  !!merge <<:
  *base
  y: 2
ref:
*base
$ python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open("t.yaml"))'
yaml.parser.ParserError: ... could not find expected ':'
```

Scalar aliases fail the same way:

```console
$ printf 'q:\n  a: &anc 1.5\n  ref: *anc\n' > s.yaml && yam s.yaml && cat s.yaml
q:
  a: &anc 1.5
  ref:
  *anc
```

These are not affected:
- an alias as a sequence item (`- *anc`)
- an alias as a mapping key (`*key : v` is reformatted as `*key: v`, which
  yaml.v3 and PyYAML both parse correctly)
- an anchor on a scalar value (`&anc 1.5`)

## Likely cause

- **(1)** In `marshalMapping`, the check that decides whether a value goes on
  the same line as its key (`encoder.go:343`) only allows non-null scalars and
  flow-style nodes. A `yaml.AliasNode` falls through to the "block value"
  branch, which writes `key:\n`. The value is then marshaled by the `default:`
  case of `marshal()` but not indented, because `applyIndent` only runs for
  mapping and sequence values. Treating `item.Kind == yaml.AliasNode` as an
  inline value at line 343 should fix this.
- **(2)** `marshalMapping` and `marshalSequence` build their output by hand
  and never write `node.Anchor`. Scalars keep their anchors only because they
  go through `yaml.Marshal`. The anchor (`&name`) needs to be written after
  the parent key's colon, or after `- ` for a sequence item, before the
  newline that starts the block.
- **(3)** Not investigated yet. The `<<` key node has the tag `!!merge` and is
  marshaled on its own through `yaml.Marshal`, which writes the tag
  explicitly.

## Failing test

`TestAliases` in `pkg/yam/formatted/encoder_test.go` is a table test in the
same style as `TestKeyComments`. Each row checks that the formatted output
matches the expected text, that it still parses, and that it decodes to the
same data as the input:

| case | status on main |
|---|---|
| alias as a top-level mapping value | FAIL (invalid YAML) |
| alias as a nested mapping value | FAIL (invalid YAML) |
| alias to a mapping as a mapping value | FAIL (anchor dropped, invalid YAML) |
| merge key with an alias | FAIL (anchor dropped, `!!merge`, invalid YAML) |
| anchor and alias on a sequence value | FAIL (anchor dropped, invalid YAML) |
| alias as a sequence item | PASS |
| alias as a mapping key | PASS |

The test can go in with the fix PR:

```go
func TestAliases(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		input string
		want  string
	}{{
		name: "alias as a top-level mapping value",
		input: `a: &anc 1.5
ref: *anc
`,
		want: `a: &anc 1.5
ref: *anc
`,
	}, {
		name: "alias as a nested mapping value",
		input: `q:
  a: &anc 1.5
  ref: *anc
`,
		want: `q:
  a: &anc 1.5
  ref: *anc
`,
	}, {
		name: "alias to a mapping as a mapping value",
		input: `base: &base
  x: 1
copy: *base
`,
		want: `base: &base
  x: 1
copy: *base
`,
	}, {
		// Common in docker-compose and CI configs.
		name: "merge key with an alias",
		input: `base: &base
  x: 1
derived:
  <<: *base
  y: 2
`,
		want: `base: &base
  x: 1
derived:
  <<: *base
  y: 2
`,
	}, {
		name: "alias as a sequence item",
		input: `a: &anc 1.5
list:
  - *anc
  - 2
`,
		want: `a: &anc 1.5
list:
  - *anc
  - 2
`,
	}, {
		// yaml.v3 itself emits "*key : v", but it and PyYAML both parse "*key: v".
		name: "alias as a mapping key",
		input: `k: &key name
m:
  *key : v
`,
		want: `k: &key name
m:
  *key: v
`,
	}, {
		name: "anchor and alias on a sequence value",
		input: `base: &list
  - 1
copy: *list
`,
		want: `base: &list
  - 1
copy: *list
`,
	}}

	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			root := &yaml.Node{}
			require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(tt.input), root))

			var buf bytes.Buffer
			require.NoError(t, NewEncoder(&buf).Encode(root))

			checkDiff(t, tt.want, buf.String())

			var want, got any
			require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(tt.input), &want))
			require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(buf.Bytes(), &got), "formatted output must parse:\n%s", buf.String())
			if diff := cmp.Diff(want, got); diff != "" {
				t.Errorf("formatted output decodes to different data (-want +got):\n%s", diff)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

items.title: Finite CI watch command is classified as a persistent server and cannot be awaited

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Observed behavior
A finite GitHub CLI pull-request check watcher was started through the shell tool. The harness classified it as a persistent server. Reading its result with a positive `wait_ms` returned an immediate snapshot rather than waiting for the watcher to exit.

The watcher exits when CI checks reach terminal states; it is not a server. This misclassification prevents the documented blocking collection of background results and can lead to an unfinished task reaching final-response reconciliation.

## Expected behavior
Treat finite watch commands as awaitable jobs, or provide an explicit finite-job override. Persistent-server detection should not infer that every command using a watch flag runs forever.

## Reproduction
1. Start `gh pr checks` with its watch flag for a pull request with pending checks.
2. Request shell job output with a positive `wait_ms`.
3. Observe the persistent-server classification and immediate snapshot.

No local identifiers, trace contents, repository-specific logs, or conversation content are included.

## Failure
A finite `gh pr checks --watch` command was classified by the shell tool as a persistent server. Calling `action=output` with a positive `wait_ms` therefore returned immediately with `running — persistent server` instead of waiting for check completion.

## Expected
A check watcher exits when all checks complete and should support a finite wait. It is not a long-lived server.

## Workaround
Running the watcher from a short Python subprocess wrapper lets the shell tool treat the outer command as a finite job.

items.title: [duplicate of #10598; graph owned by #10596] tooling(lsp4ij): emit bounded agent packets and checked graph projections
items.body:
Parent/controller: #10550
Train predecessors: C01–C04 control-plane leaves
Programme: #8539 / #7873

## Train position

**C05 — agent execution packets and generated projections.** Begins after the manifest, validator, current-tree status, and offline frontier are merged.

## One-PR outcome

Implement deterministic projections equivalent to:

```bash
cargo xtask integration lsp4ij train explain <issue-or-node>
cargo xtask integration lsp4ij train graph
```

`explain` gives a coding agent one complete bounded implementation packet. `graph` generates the checked human-readable train and DOT/Mermaid projection from the same machine authority. Neither command schedules work, queries GitHub, edits issue bodies, or makes implementation/evidence/support decisions.

## Agent packet contract

For one node emit, in this order:

```text
node / issue / one-PR result
why this node is ready or blocked now
controller chain and programme lane
exact current-main/tree subject
hard, evidence, and external dependencies
canonical authorities to consume
writer slot and conflict key
maximum evidence stage and claim ceiling
allowed write surfaces
forbidden adjacent work
expected production/test/generated surfaces
first discriminating failing test or fixture
positive proof and realistic false-green controls
focused verification commands
required generated artifacts/receipts
rollback boundary
stop, split, transfer, and supersession conditions
following nodes newly unblocked on success
PR title/body contract
handoff/closeout fields
```

The packet is usable by a cheap coding model without reading every controller, but it must retain links/digests to those authorities and may not restate their semantics inconsistently.

## Cheap-model safety rules

Packets must use direct bounded instructions rather than open-ended repository exploration:

- name the one result, not a theme;
- name exact prerequisite facts to verify on current `main`;
- name the existing components/helpers to reuse;
- list forbidden replacement authorities explicitly;
- identify likely files or owned directories without making them exclusive when current code moved;
- state the falsifier before the implementation direction;
- state which failures transfer to another owner;
- require fresh proof after final edits;
- require a blocked handoff instead of weakening a gate.

Do not embed volatile live PR/check/review facts in the offline packet.

## Blocked/transfer handoff

For a blocked or stopped node emit a compact receipt containing:

```text
exact inspected tree and node contract
first blocking term
observed evidence
work performed, if any
files/fixtures changed or untouched
salvageable patch/branch reference supplied externally
canonical transfer owner
why the current node must not absorb the repair
```

This is a local report shape, not a branch/PR mutation.

## Graph projection

Generate one checked Markdown plus DOT or Mermaid view containing:

- controllers versus leaves;
- hard/evidence/external edges with distinct notation;
- writer slots/conflict keys;
- evidence stages and claim ceilings;
- current-tree implementation states;
- superseded/transferred history;
- external-release gates;
- the current offline frontier.

No second hand-maintained train document may become authoritative. Generated order and node/edge IDs are deterministic.

## PR metadata contract

The packet includes a copy-ready PR body skeleton:

```text
Closes/Relates
Parent train and row
Exact base/head
One result
Authorities consumed
Implementation
Falsifiers and proof
Claim boundary
Limitations / not-proven cells
Rollback
Following node
```

It does not publish the PR.

## Falsifiers

Fail when:

- a packet omits the one-PR result, authority, falsifier, rollback, or stop condition;
- a controller is rendered as an implementation packet;
- a blocked node is presented as ready;
- live GitHub facts enter deterministic offline output;
- a packet permits a second launcher/fixture/receipt/installer/registry/capability authority;
- generated graph and manifest disagree;
- one evidence stage is described as another;
- a packet tells an agent to keep working through a canonical transfer boundary;
- repeated packet/graph generation changes without semantic movement.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `train explain` produces one complete bounded agent packet for every implementation leaf.
- [ ] Ready, blocked, superseded, transferred, and external-gated packets remain distinct.
- [ ] Cheap-model instructions name exact reuse, writes, proof, falsifiers, stop/transfer, and closeout.
- [ ] A blocked handoff preserves useful work without widening scope.
- [ ] `train graph` is generated from the canonical authority and deterministic.
- [ ] PR metadata skeletons preserve exact subject, proof, and claim boundaries.
- [ ] No scheduler, GitHub query/mutation, branch/PR creation, host run, merge decision, or support promotion exists.

## Verification

```bash
cargo test -p xtask --locked lsp4ij_train_explain
cargo test -p xtask --locked lsp4ij_train_graph
cargo xtask integration lsp4ij train check
cargo xtask integration lsp4ij train graph --check
cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check
```

## Codex goal prompt

Implement deterministic `train explain` and `train graph` projections over the merged control-plane authorities. Make each leaf packet complete enough for a cheap model: one result, exact prerequisites and authorities, allowed/forbidden writes, first falsifier, proof, claim ceiling, rollback, stop/transfer rules, following node, and PR body skeleton. Generate one checked graph with typed edges and current-tree states. Do not query or mutate GitHub, schedule work, run hosts, or promote support.

## Non-goals

No issue-body publisher, remote agent launcher, task lease, live PR observer, review/CI admission, or external write.

items.title: [DUPLICATE of #1553] security(MEDIUM): registro da primeira passkey WebAuthn sem autenticação permite sequestro de dashboard

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — must fix before next stable tag

items.body:
## Achado (Cursor Vulnerability Scanner, `#data-boar-ops`, run `bc-c11a220d-8810-4ba3-92c5-ead2f49f8b57`, scan 2026-07-11T02:10:57-07:00)

**Severidade: MEDIUM** — confirmado presente em `main` (verificado 2026-08-12). Parte do lote "12 previously flagged" do data-boar; sem issue prévia.

### Problema

`api/webauthn_routes.py:72-76` — `POST /auth/webauthn/registration/options` só checa `dbm.webauthn_credential_count() > 0`; nenhuma autenticação é exigida. `/auth/*` é explicitamente isento do middleware de API key (`optional_api_key_middleware`). Quando WebAuthn está habilitado mas nenhuma passkey foi registrada ainda (janela de bootstrap após install fresh ou wipe de credencial), qualquer cliente com acesso de rede consegue registrar a primeira passkey sem autenticação nenhuma. `registration_verify` (linha 113) também não re-checa a contagem antes de salvar — TOCTOU adicional.

### Impacto

Atacante na rede registra a primeira passkey FIDO2 antes do operador legítimo. O atacante ganha um cookie de sessão assinado (`db_webauthn`, 7 dias) concedendo acesso ao dashboard HTML. Quando API key não está configurada (default), isso escala pra acesso completo de escrita de config via `POST /{locale}/config`. O operador legítimo fica trancado fora e precisa de recuperação de credencial fora de banda.

### Caminho de ataque

1. Atacante identifica instância Data Boar com `api.webauthn.enabled: true` e zero passkeys registradas (install fresh ou pós-wipe)
2. Atacante envia `POST /auth/webauthn/registration/options` — sem API key exigida; endpoint retorna challenge FIDO2 já que `webauthn_credential_count() == 0`
3. Atacante completa a cerimônia FIDO2 via `POST /auth/webauthn/registration/verify` com seu próprio autenticador
4. Servidor salva a credencial do atacante e retorna cookie de sessão assinado com o user ID default (single-operator mode)
5. Gate HTML Phase 1b passa a exigir auth por cookie em todas as rotas do dashboard — operador legítimo vê redirect pro login
6. Operador legítimo chama `registration/options` e recebe 403 ("A passkey is already registered")
7. Com API key não configurada (default), o cookie de sessão do atacante concede acesso a `POST /{locale}/config` pra controle total de configuração

### Evidência

- `api/webauthn_routes.py:72-76` — `registration_options()` só checa `webauthn_credential_count() > 0`; nenhuma autenticação exigida
- `api/webauthn_routes.py:113-158` — `registration_verify()` salva credencial e emite cookie de sessão sem check de auth prévio, sem re-checar contagem
- `optional_api_key_middleware` — isenta todos os paths `/auth/` do requisito de API key

### Remediação sugerida

Exigir autenticação por API key (ou um token de setup único) no primeiro registro WebAuthn quando a instância faz bind em interface não-loopback. Alternativamente, adicionar guard TOCTOU em `registration_verify` que re-checa `webauthn_credential_count() == 0` antes de salvar a credencial, e considerar uma janela de bootstrap time-limited com secret de setup.

PoC em vídeo não é viável — o exploit exige um dispositivo autenticador FIDO2 ou autenticador de plataforma e uma instância Data Boar rodando com WebAuthn habilitado; o ataque é uma sequência de requisições HTTP padrão sem interação visual de UI.

---
*Achado por Cursor Vulnerability Scanner via Slack `#data-boar-ops`; verificado contra o código atual em `main` antes de abrir esta issue.*

items.title: Hook test: the worktree-add post-bash case fails inside every ir-* worktree

labels.name: kind: dev-experience
labels.description: The harness, build, CI, rules and tooling for whoever works on the repo

labels.name: area: platform
labels.description: deck-core, adapters, plugins, native addons, build and release tooling

items.body:
## Problem

`scripts/claude-hooks/post-bash.test.mjs` › "moves the card of the tree the add created, not of one a comment names" (added in #1321) passes in the `master` checkout and in CI, but fails in every `ir-<issue>` worktree, so every worktree session's full `pnpm test` shows one red that has nothing to do with its own change:

```text
AssertionError: expected '[hook] Worktree for #1336 created, bu…' to match /Worktree for #1321 created/
```

Two causes combine:

1. **The test fires the hook from the wrong cwd.** `fire()` passes `cwd: import.meta.dirname` (`<checkout>/scripts/claude-hooks`), so the command's `../ir-1321` resolves to `<checkout>/scripts/ir-1321` — a path a real `git worktree add` from the repo root never produces.
2. **`issueFromWorktreePath` (`rules-post.mjs`) takes the FIRST `ir-<n>` segment of the path.** From `master` that is `…/master/scripts/ir-1321` → 1321; from a worktree it is `…/ir-1336/scripts/ir-1321` → 1336.

Real use is unaffected: a real add runs from a repo root and resolves to a sibling, and CI's checkout is not named `ir-*`.

## Change

- Fire the worktree-add case from a repo-root cwd (or an absolute target), so the resolved path is the shape the hook really sees.
- Make `issueFromWorktreePath` read the worktree's own folder — the LAST `ir-<n>` segment, or the basename — rather than the first match, with a test where an `ir-<n>` ancestor encloses the target.
- Positive control: the case must fail on today's code when run from a path containing an `ir-<n>` ancestor, and pass after.

## Affected artifacts

- `scripts/claude-hooks/post-bash.test.mjs`, `scripts/claude-hooks/rules-post.mjs` (+ its test)
- `.claude/rules/hooks.md` only if the described behaviour changes

## Out of scope

Any other hook behaviour.

### Description

When using the new v2 layout (`newLayoutDesigns: true`) and switching conversation tabs, no sound plays and no in-app toast appears when a background session requests a permission or asks a question.

The legacy layout works fine, but the new layout is missing the event listener that handles `permission.asked` and `question.asked` events entirely.

A secondary issue: even in the legacy layout, `question.asked` events (agent needs an answer) never play a sound — only system notifications fire.

1. Use the new v2 interface (Settings → enabled by default for new installs)
2. Start an agent in one tab
3. Switch to a different conversation tab
4. Wait for the agent to request a permission or ask a question
5. No sound plays, no in-app toast appears

items.title: Cancel answers 202 even when nothing was cancelled

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Summary

`POST /eve/v1/session/:id/cancel` returns `202 {status: "accepted"}` when the session has no open turn, and also when the body names a `turnId` that is not the open turn. In both cases nothing is cancelled and no event follows, so the response cannot tell a caller whether its Stop took effect.

The route already has a `no_active_turn` response, but `Session.cancel()` (`channel/session.ts`) only dispatches a `cancel` command to the session inbox and reports `accepted` once the inbox takes it; the session workflow then drops the command when no turn is open or the `turnId` does not match (`active-turn.ts` `cancelsThisTurn`). Still the same on `main` (8136e50).

## Reproduction (eve 0.70.2, unpatched, local World, mock model)

1. Idle session: create a session, wait for `turn.completed` → `session.waiting`, then `POST /cancel` with `{}`. Response: `202 {"ok":true,"status":"accepted"}`. The stream gets no new event.
2. Mismatched turn: while a `ctx.ask` question holds `turn_0`, `POST /cancel` with `{"turnId":"turn_9"}`. Response: `202`. The question stays pending; answering it later continues `turn_0` to `turn.completed` as if no cancel had been sent.
3. For comparison, the same held turn with `POST /cancel` `{}` → `202`, then `input.resolved [cancelled]` → `turn.cancelled` → `session.waiting`. Only this case did anything.

## Expected

The response says whether a turn was cancelled, for example `202 {"status":"accepted","turnId":"turn_0"}` when one was, and `409 {"code":"no_active_turn"}` (or `200 {"status":"not_required"}`) when the session is idle or the named turn is not the open one.

## Actual

Always `202 {"status":"accepted"}`.

## Why it matters

An app that shows Stop has to prove the outcome from the stream (wait for `turn.cancelled`, or for the turn's natural end) instead of trusting the response, and it cannot distinguish "the turn ended before my cancel arrived" from "my cancel was lost". We do the stream proof today, but the API invites the mistake.

## Suggested fix

In the cancel route, resolve the target first: no open turn → `not_required`/409; a `turnId` that differs from the open turn → 409 with the open turn id; otherwise cancel and return the cancelled `turnId`. Keeping 202 for the real cancellation keeps existing clients working.

items.title: subagent: parent sees premature completion when a child yields on a background command
items.body:
### Description

A subagent that ends its turn while a background shell command it started is still running is reported to its parent as `completed`, with its last-written text (often "I'll be notified when it finishes"). When the command later finishes, the child session wakes and produces a new message, but the parent is never notified. The parent's "final response" is therefore premature and can be contradicted by output it never sees. Happens for both foreground and `background: true` subagents.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Spawn a subagent (foreground or `background: true`) and have it run a long command via `shell` with `background: true`, then end its turn.
2. The subagent job settles as `completed` immediately and returns the "I'll be notified…" text to the parent.
3. When the command finishes, the child session wakes and produces another assistant message.
4. The parent is not notified of that message.

### Expected behavior

Either the subagent job does not settle `completed` while it has outstanding background work it started, or the parent is notified when the child resumes with a new result.

### Actual behavior

The subagent job settles on child session idle. The completion observer is armed once per spawn generation, and shell completion wakes only the child session, so nothing re-arms a parent notification when the child resumes.

### Plugins

-opencode.browser

### OpenCode version

v2.0.21

### Operating System

Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 (x64)

### Terminal

xterm-256color

items.title: 11.28.3 regression: skipped optional platform packages are symlinked to the project root, creating a symlink loop

labels.name: area: monorepo
labels.description: Everything related to the pnpm workspace feature

items.body:
### Last pnpm version that worked

11.28.2

### pnpm version

11.28.3

### Code to reproduce the issue

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
echo '{"name":"root","private":true,"packageManager":"pnpm@11.28.3"}' > package.json
printf 'packages:\n  - packages/*\nallowBuilds:\n  esbuild: false\n' > pnpm-workspace.yaml
mkdir -p packages/app packages/other
echo '{"name":"app","version":"1.0.0","dependencies":{"esbuild":"0.25.12"}}' > packages/app/package.json
echo '{"name":"other","version":"1.0.0"}' > packages/other/package.json
pnpm install
ls -l node_modules/.pnpm/esbuild@0.25.12/node_modules/@esbuild/
```

### Expected behavior

Only the host's platform package is linked, as with 11.28.2:

```
linux-x64 -> ../../../@esbuild+linux-x64@0.25.12/node_modules/@esbuild/linux-x64
```

### Actual behavior

Every skipped platform package of `esbuild` (25 entries: `aix-ppc64`, `darwin-arm64`, `win32-x64`, …) is created as a symlink to `../../../../..`, which resolves to the project root:

```
aix-ppc64 -> ../../../../..
android-arm -> ../../../../..
...
linux-x64 -> ../../../@esbuild+linux-x64@0.25.12/node_modules/@esbuild/linux-x64
...
win32-x64 -> ../../../../..
```

Anything that walks `node_modules` then hits a symlink loop. A Next.js 16 (Turbopack) production build fails during output file tracing with:

```
Error [TurbopackInternalError]: Failed to write app endpoint /sitemap.xml/route
Caused by:
- 'node_modules/.pnpm/esbuild@0.25.12/node_modules/@esbuild/aix-ppc64' is a symlink causes that causes an infinite loop!
```

### Additional information

- Happens with both a plain `pnpm install` and a filtered one (`pnpm install --filter 'app...'`) in a workspace. A single-project (non-workspace) install with the same dependency did not reproduce it.
- Same reproduction counting the `../../../../..` links: 0 on 11.25.0, 11.27.1, 11.28.0, 11.28.2, 12.8.1 and 12.8.2; 25 on 11.28.3. So this looks specific to 11.28.3.
- Also reproduced on CI (Linux x64 build machines) with a frozen-lockfile install of a larger workspace.

### Node.js version

24.15.0 (also seen on Node 22 in CI)

### Operating System

Linux

items.title: Setting CARGO_BUILD_WARNINGS=deny turns linker_messages into hard error
items.body:
The `linker_messages` warning is special in rustc, it remains a warning even under `-D warnings`. This was done because linkers can warn for all sorts of reasons, and the warnings can be hard to understand or non-actionable. For instance, building Miri on macOS in CI prints a bunch of
```
  warning: linker stderr: '+zcm' is not a recognized feature for this target (ignoring feature)
           '+zcz'+zcm' is not a recognized feature for this target (ignoring feature)
           '+zcz' is not a recognized feature for this target (ignoring feature)
           ' is not a recognized feature for this target (ignoring feature)
           '+zcm' is not a recognized feature for this target (ignoring feature)
           '+zcz' is not a recognized feature for this target (ignoring feature)
```
(That specific problem is tracked in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/161561.)

However, unfortunately it seems like `CARGO_BUILD_WARNINGS=deny` will indiscriminately turn all warnings into hard errors, even those where the compiler goes out of its way to make them not hard errors. That's somewhat incoherent, and it kind of undermines the decision we made to *not* have these warnings be hard errors even with `-D warnings`.

Also see [this Zulip discussion](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/linker.20warnings/with/580632217r).
Cc @jyn514

items.title: [RETRACTED — duplicate of #8937, wrong diagnosis] merge-queue failure on #8933 attributed to #8935's preset refusal
items.body:
**⛔ Shared damage — `main` appears to be red, which blocks every PR in the merge queue.** Filed unassigned and ungraded for triage, immediately, by the `domain:metadata`/`engine-core`/`drivers` seat (PM session `session_01XeQRiAa7vYRVX5Fog7Zby8`).

## How it surfaced

The merge-queue build for PR #8933 (an unrelated `metadata-protocol` change) failed. The queue runs the **full** suite; PR-side CI runs only the affected subset — so the failing test is in a package #8933 never touched:

```
FAIL src/engine-temporal-comparand-door.test.ts
  > [#8690] the temporal-comparand door at the engine collection point
  > refuses the card's comparands with code AND status, while the positive control still returns 38
```

#8933 has been dequeued (`CI_FAILURE`) through no fault of its own. ⛔ It must **not** be blindly re-queued — per the merge-queue-triage workflow's own checklist, a re-queue on an unrelated failure burns a full rebuild for every PR behind it.

## Diagnosis — strong evidence, ⛔ NOT a executed run

Stating the confidence precisely, because I have not run the test myself.

**Three commits landed on `main` between #8933's base (`3315d1d4`) and now (`716ac9bf8`)** — measured:

- `a77794427` — **#8793 / PR #8935**, *"refuse a bare date-range preset name in an ordering filter comparand at publish time"*
- `716ac9bf8` — #8790 / PR #8927 (`driver-sql`)
- `2c86fe3ea` — #8715 / PR #8932 (`spec`, ApiKeySchema)

⛔ **Nothing touching the temporal-comparand door or its inputs landed in that window** (`git log` over `temporal-comparand-door.ts`, `core/src/utils/temporal-comparand.ts` and the test file returns empty). So the door's own code did not change.

**What #8935 did change** is `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts` (+134), adding a **schema-level** refusal:

```
// 3.35 Bare date-range preset names in ordering comparands — REFUSED (#8793)
const PRESET_JUDGED_ORDERING_OPS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['$gt', '$gte', '$lt', '$lte']);
```

**What the failing test asserts** (`engine-temporal-comparand-door.test.ts:132-141`):

```ts
it("refuses the card's comparands with code AND status, while the positive control still returns 38", …)
  expect(err!.code).toBe('INVALID_FILTER');
  expect(err!.status).toBe(400);
```

⇒ `$gte "last_30_days"` is **exactly** a declared preset name in an ordering position. #8935 now refuses it at the **schema** layer, before it reaches the engine collection point where #8690's door raises `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. Same input, two refusals, and the earlier one wins — so the door's pin no longer observes what it was written to observe.

## Why no gate caught it, and why that is the reusable part

This is the **spec-consumer fixture hazard** stated in the PM playbook in almost these words: *a change in package A can make package B's fixture assert the opposite, and no sweep inside `spec` can see it.*

#8935 is a `spec` + `lint` change. Its consumption radius includes **`objectql`**, which is where this door and its pin live. A `spec`-scoped verification — however thorough — is structurally blind to this.

## ⚠️ My share of this, stated rather than left for someone to find

**I carved #8793 out of #8690 myself**, into the `domain:spec` lane, precisely so the C half would run at its mandatory tier. In that carve-out card I wrote that the two are *"two refusals at two boundaries, not one refusal split across packages."*

That framing was right about ownership and **wrong about interaction**: I did not flag that the C half's refusal fires on the **same input** as the B half's, at an **earlier** boundary, and would therefore invalidate the B half's pins. The spec seat had no reason to know it needed `objectql` in its consumption radius, because my carve-out card did not tell it. That is a PM error, not a dev error, and the corrective belongs in how cross-boundary carve-outs are written: **when one card's refusal precedes another's on the same input, the carve-out must name the earlier one's pins as the later one's consumption radius.**

## What a fix has to decide

⛔ Not "delete the assertion." The question is which boundary owns the refusal for this input, and both rulings are live:

1. **Schema-first (accept #8935's behaviour as correct)** — then #8690's door pin is re-pointed to assert the *schema's* refusal for preset names, and keeps its own door-level assertions for the comparands the schema does **not** judge (`not-a-date-at-all`, a bare non-preset string). The door is still load-bearing — #8935's own comment says so explicitly (*"the engine door still refuses these at query time, with the field's type in hand"*) — so this is a pin-scoping fix, not a deletion.
2. **Door-first** — #8935's schema refusal is narrowed so the engine door keeps this input. Costlier and contradicts a ruling that just landed.
3. Both, with the door pin asserting *whichever* fires — ⛔ rejected on sight: a pin that accepts either answer cannot detect the boundary moving again.

**(1) is the obvious reading** and #8935's own prose supports it, but it is a two-ruling question and I am not adjudicating it from this seat.

## Immediate

- ⛔ Do not re-queue #8933 (or anything else) until this is green — the queue will keep failing on the full suite.
- Verification owed by whoever takes this: **run `engine-temporal-comparand-door.test.ts` on current `main`** and confirm red before changing anything. Everything above is read from diffs and the queue log; I have not executed it.

Refs: #8690 (B half, the engine door) · #8793 / PR #8935 (C half, the schema refusal) · PR #8933 (the innocent PR the queue failed) · the merge-queue-triage workflow (#4859) whose checklist this follows.

items.title: Settings: treat bambuddy_render_api_key (SCADBUDDY_BAMBUDDY_RENDER_API_KEY) as a secret

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Problem

`bambuddy_render_api_key` is the Manage-Library-only key that render workers hold (spec §9, phase 3 plan). The backend already treats it as write-only: it's never returned, only `has_render_api_key` is. The Settings page doesn't:

- `SettingsPage.tsx` has `const SECRETS = ['bambuddy_api_key', 'google_fonts_api_key']`, and the render key isn't in it.
- It isn't in `RUNTIME_FIELDS` either. So `extraSpecs()` shows it in **Diagnostics** with the raw label `SCADBUDDY_BAMBUDDY_RENDER_API_KEY`, as a plain `text` input. It also doesn't appear in `hasKey()` / `serverValue()`.

The result is a plain-text box that is never masked. You can't tell whether a key is stored, there's no **Remove key** button, and saving the box empty sends `null` instead of following the secret rule ("omitted when untouched").

## Fix

- Add it to the secrets handling: `SECRETS`, `hasKey()` (→ `has_render_api_key`) and `serverValue()` (always `''`).
- Use a `type="password"` input with `autoComplete="off"`. The placeholder should say "A key is stored. Paste a new one to replace it." when `has_render_api_key` is true, and there should be a **Remove key** button. Both are `USER_ONLY`.
- Move it to **Connection**, under the main API key. Label it "Render worker API key". Help text: "Needs only Manage Library. Render workers run template code, so they get this key instead of the full one."
- When `render_key_fallback` is true, show a persistent warning: "render workers hold the full Bambuddy key; template code can print" (spec §9).
- Show the source badge and reset as for other env-seeded fields.
- Agent tools must never read or set it (same as `bambuddy_api_key`).

Longer term, #889 makes `secret` a schema-declared kind, so this can't happen again. This issue is the immediate fix.

## Related

#889 (typed settings schema), #887 (friendly names / env var shown), and the separate issue for a Rotate button.

items.title: Persist ~/.claude/projects from the agent container so session transcripts survive
items.body:
Raised at the owner's request (live chat: "ok raise an issue to link up projects too so that it gets persisted").

## Problem
Diagnosing credfeto/recommendations-defi-dashboard#419 (see #1557) needed the agent session transcripts to find out why 62 commands were denied across seven sessions. None existed. `lib/podman` persists only `sessions session-env plans cache backups` from the container's `~/.claude` (the two `for d in ...` loops around lines 776 and 833: one `mkdir -p` on the host, one `--volume` mount). `projects/`, where Claude Code writes `<session-id>.jsonl` transcripts, is missing from that list. Separately, `~/.claude` in the image is root-owned, so the container cannot create `projects/` itself (#1365).

## Proposed change
- Add `projects` to both loops in `lib/podman`, so the host creates `${CLAUDE_STATE_DIR}/projects` and mounts it read-write at `/home/developer/.claude/projects`. The mount point then exists and is writable by `developer` without making `~/.claude` itself writable, which keeps the lockdown #1365's discussion asks to keep.
- Add a bats assertion alongside the existing mount-list tests, and update `docs/development/` (and `ai/local/debugging.instructions.md`'s state inventory) to name the transcript location: `/home/<owner>/.local/state/orchestrator/<owner>/<repo>/claude/projects/`.
- Check that the image's sanity checks or `entrypoint.sh` don't assume the old directory set.
- Consider pruning: transcripts grow with every session, so either age them out (like the image pruning) or document the expected growth.

## Acceptance
After one agent run on nanoclaw, a `<session-id>.jsonl` for that run exists under the repo's `claude/projects/` directory on the host and survives the container's `--rm`.

Related: #1365 (container-side root-owned `~/.claude`), #1557.

items.title: Release profile broken with Maven 3.10.0 (missing javadoc JARs)
items.body:
The `release` profile in `quarkiverse-parent` is activated by `-DperformRelease`:

```xml
<profile>
  <id>release</id>
  <activation>
    <property>
      <name>performRelease</name>
    </property>
  </activation>
  ...
</profile>
```

Maven 3.10.0 no longer honors `-DperformRelease` for profile activation, so the `maven-javadoc-plugin` execution inside this profile never runs. This causes Central deploy failures with `*-javadoc.jar is missing`.

**Confirmed affected repos:**
- `quarkus-web-bundler` 2.3.5
- `quarkus-reactive-messaging-nats-jetstream` 3.40.0

Any Quarkiverse repo that adopts the Maven 3.10.0 wrapper will be affected.

**Suggested fix:** Move the `maven-javadoc-plugin` execution out of the `release` profile into `<build><plugins>`, like `maven-source-plugin` already is. Alternatively, change the profile activation to use a different property name.

items.title: hydrolysis: a material allocates a full-resolution backdrop capture beside its quarter-scale one

labels.name: performance
labels.description: Runtime performance: rendering, layout, memory, binary size

items.body:
## What happened

`a_material_installs_a_quarter_scale_colour_then_blur_backdrop_group` in `backends/hydrolysis/src/renderer/tests/material.rs` fails on `dev` at 936d2ad14. The assertion `bytes == 80 * 60 * 8` ("the capture is a quarter of the window") gets 652800 instead of 38400.

652800 is 38400 plus 614400, and 614400 is a full 320×240 `rgba16float` capture. So besides the quarter-scale capture the material group asks for, the engine now holds a full-resolution backdrop capture for the same window.

The dev push gate compiles but does not run the test suite, so the failure did not block the merges that introduced it. The candidates, all recent on dev: #1956 (material levels as a backdrop treatment), 8cf42240c (blur material backdrops in encoded sRGB), and #1976 (a backdrop capture looks through translucent levels).

## Reproduction

`cargo nextest run -p hydrolysis --features accessibility,testing,winit -E 'test(a_material_installs_a_quarter_scale_colour_then_blur_backdrop_group)'`

## Affected surface

`backends/hydrolysis` material backdrop install, and the `cherenkov` backdrop capture allocation.

## Additional context

The test is the regression check that a material costs a quarter-resolution capture only. If a full-resolution capture is now allocated beside it, every material pays about 16 times the intended capture memory.

items.title: [Bug]: Users table fails to load with German locale in v8.8.0 due to invalid JavaScript
items.body:
### Snipe-IT Version v8.8.0 - build 25378 (master) ### PHP Version PHP 8.3.6 (cli) (built: Sep 2 2026 12:56:02) (NTS) Zend Engine v4.3.6 with Zend OPcache v8.3.6 ### Composer Version Composer version 2.10.3 2026-08-27 13:34:23 PHP version 8.3.6 (/usr/bin/php8.3) ### MySQL/MariaDB version MariaDB 11.8.9 ### How did you install Snipe-IT? Docker ### Is this a fresh install or an upgrade? Upgrade ### What happened? After upgrading to Snipe-IT v8.8.0, the Users page stops working when the user locale is set to German (`de-DE`). The page itself loads successfully, but the users table is not initialized and no request to: ```text /api/v1/users?deleted=false ``` is sent. The browser console shows: ```text Uncaught SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token at users:1354:27 ``` The issue disappears immediately when switching the user language from German to English. LDAP synchronization itself still works correctly and users are present in the database. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run Snipe-IT v8.8.0 build 25378. 2. Set the user locale to German (`de-DE`). 3. Open `/users`. 4. The users table remains empty and is not initialized. 5. Open the browser console. 6. The following error appears: ```text Uncaught SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token at users:1354:27 ``` 7. Switch the user locale to English. 8. Open `/users` again. 9. The users table works normally. ### Expected behavior The Users table should load normally regardless of the selected locale. ### Actual behavior With the German locale enabled, the generated JavaScript becomes syntactically invalid and execution of the page script stops before Bootstrap Table initialization. ### Technical details The problem appears to be caused by the localized Advanced Search help text being inserted directly into a single-quoted JavaScript string. The generated page contains code similar to: ```javascript html.push('

... Für spezifischere Ergebnisse können Sie ... is_not:value für einen exakten Ausschluss, is:null für leere Werte ...

'); ``` The German translation contains a real newline inside the single-quoted JavaScript string. This causes the browser parser to fail with: ```text Uncaught SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token ``` Since the script stops parsing at that point, the Bootstrap Table initialization is never executed and the users API request is never sent. ### Additional confirmation Changing the user locale from German to English immediately fixes the issue without any other configuration changes. LDAP synchronization continues to work in both locales. ### Browser Google Chrome 150 on macOS. ### Workaround Switching the user locale to English restores the Users table. ### What browsers are you seeing the problem on? Chrome ### Can you reproduce this on the public demo? No ### Do you have full multiple company support enabled? No ### If you have full multiple company support enabled, do you have location scoping to company enabled? I do not have full multiple company support enabled ### Application log output ```shell No relevant application log errors were found for this issue. The /users page itself returns HTTP 200 and LDAP synchronization works correctly. The failure occurs client-side while parsing the generated JavaScript. ``` ### Browser console output ```shell Uncaught SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token (at users:1354:27) The error occurs in the generated JavaScript for the Advanced Search help text when the locale is set to de-DE. The generated JavaScript contains a literal newline inside a single-quoted string: html.push('

... is_not:value für einen exakten Ausschluss, is:null für leere Werte ...

'); Switching the user locale to English makes the error disappear and the Users table loads normally. ``` ### Common Issues - [x] I have searched this repo for existing issues related to my issue (including closed issues) - [x] My APP_URL is set correctly in my .env file (including http or https and no trailing slash) - [x] I have searched the official Snipe-IT documentation and have checked the Common Issues documentation (where applicable) - [x] I have run database migrations (where applicable). - [x] I have attached screenshots and/or videos of the issue (where applicable) ### Code of Conduct - [x] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

items.title: CI: perf-metrics artifact upload timeout turns a passing docker-test red
items.body:
## Problem

The `docker-test` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ends with an "Upload perf metrics artifacts" step (`actions/upload-artifact@v4`, `if: always()`) that uploads `metrics_history.json` and the benchmark PNGs as a trend artifact. That artifact is a convenience for inspecting page-load trends; nothing gates on it.

On experimental commit d2e33cc, CI run [36646344880](https://github.com/Young-Supernova-Experiment/YSE_PZ/actions/runs/36646344880) attempt 1 went red even though the Django system check, the full test suite, and the page-load regression/benchmark step had all passed. The only failure was the upload step: `actions/upload-artifact` hit five consecutive GitHub ArtifactService `CreateArtifact` timeouts and gave up. A plain rerun of the same commit went green with no code change.

## Impact

A transient failure in GitHub's artifact backend marks the whole job failed, which:

- shows a red check on a commit whose code is fine,
- blocks anyone treating the `docker-test` check as a merge signal until someone notices and reruns,
- costs a full ~20-minute rerun of the Docker stack just to re-upload a non-essential file.

## Fix

Mark the upload step advisory with `continue-on-error: true` so a failed upload is reported as a warning on the job instead of failing it. All test and benchmark steps keep their current gating behaviour. This is the only `upload-artifact` step in the repository's workflows, so no sibling steps need the same treatment.

---

items.title: Version and publish the workspace status JSON contract

milestone.title: v1.10.0
milestone.description: Follow-up work carried forward from the v1.9.0 milestone.

items.body:
## Goal

Make `basectl workspace status --format json` a versioned, documented automation contract before v1.10.0.

## Background

Release-preparation review on 2026-10-05 against Base main `f662bc75e955a46c3ad1beba70b7e4a179bba6d7`.

Base's stability policy says that object-shaped JSON intended for automation must include `schema_version` (`docs/stability-tiers.md` lines 55-59). The workspace status documentation calls its JSON output a stable JSON document and describes its top-level fields (`docs/output-formats.md` lines 35-38), but `workspace_status_to_json` builds the payload without that key (`cli/python/base_projects/workspace_report_json.py` lines 23-35). The existing JSON test checks status, counts, and project fields but never asserts the version (`cli/python/base_projects/tests/test_engine.py` lines 577-613). There is also no `docs/schemas/workspace-status.json` while the workspace test and update payloads have published schemas.

This is reproducible without a live workspace:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from base_projects.workspace_report_json import workspace_status_to_json

payload = workspace_status_to_json(
    Path("/tmp/workspace"),
    (SimpleNamespace(
        name="demo", status="ok", root=Path("/tmp/workspace/demo"),
        manifest_path=None, venv="not_applicable", manifest="valid",
        last_check=None, issues=[], python_runtime=None,
    ),),
)
assert "schema_version" not in payload
```

The public `basectl workspace status --format json` path emits the same unversioned object, so consumers cannot apply the repository's stated schema-evolution rule to this stable command.

## Scope

- Add `schema_version: 1` to the workspace status JSON envelope.
- Publish a schema for the status payload alongside the other workspace schemas, or explicitly document why a shared schema is the intended contract.
- Extend focused tests to assert the version and validate the documented payload shape.
- Update `docs/output-formats.md`, `docs/command-reference.md`, and `docs/stability-tiers.md` links/listings so the status contract is discoverable and consistent with workspace test/update.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `basectl workspace status --format json` emits `schema_version: 1` at the top level for empty, manifest-backed, and discovery-backed workspaces.
- [ ] A checked-in schema or equivalent normative contract covers the status envelope, project records, aggregate status enum, and optional manifest metadata.
- [ ] Tests fail before the fix and pass after it for the public engine path.
- [ ] The three user-facing documentation surfaces agree on the versioned status contract.

## Validation

Run the focused workspace status tests, the JSON/schema contract tests, `git diff --check`, and the repository release test gate.

## Non-Goals

Do not change status precedence, project discovery, exit codes, or the existing project record fields except where needed to publish the schema.

## Project Fields

- Status: Ready
- Priority: P2
- Area: Workspace
- Initiative: Contract Hardening
- Size: S
- Issue type: Bug
- Assignee: codeforester
- Milestone: v1.10.0

## Agent Assignment

Assignee: @codeforester. The reproduced output and acceptance criteria define the implementation boundary.

items.title: Add a route-level test for `POST /rebalance` returning 405 after removal.

labels.name: haiku
labels.description: Implementable by Haiku with detailed spec

items.body:
## What

Add a route-level test asserting that `POST /rebalance` returns HTTP 405 (Method Not Allowed) now that the endpoint has been deliberately removed in PR #9466.

The test should live alongside the existing route-level tests in `tests/test_app.py`, which already exercises `DELETE` against the removed route and asserts 405. Extend that coverage to `POST` on the same path.

## Why

PR #9466 removed `POST /rebalance` from `backend/routes/rebalance.py` and removed its frontend caller (`getRebalance` in `frontend/src/api.ts`). The removal is intentional, but the only route-level regression guard currently in place checks `DELETE` — not `POST`. If a future change accidentally re-registers a `POST` handler on that path (or a catch-all route starts accepting it), nothing in the test suite would catch it.

This was flagged as a non-blocking follow-up in the AI review of PR #9466 under "Test coverage" and "Suggested follow-up issues".

## How

1. Open `tests/test_app.py`.
2. Locate the existing test that calls `client.delete(path)` on the removed rebalance paths and asserts 405.
3. Add a parallel assertion (either in the same test or a new focused test) that calls `client.post(path)` on the same path(s) and asserts `response.status_code == 405`.
4. Keep the test minimal — no request body is required, since the route should not exist at all. If the framework returns 405 before body parsing, an empty body is sufficient; if a body is required to reach the routing layer, send `json={}`.
5. Do not add a new fixture or helper unless the existing test structure makes it awkward.

## Files Affected

- `tests/test_app.py`

## Constraints

- Must not change production code in `backend/routes/rebalance.py` — the endpoint is intentionally gone.
- Must not re-introduce `POST /rebalance` or any frontend caller.
- Must not break the existing `DELETE` → 405 assertion in the same file.
- Out of scope: the other follow-ups from the same review (orphaned `suggest_trades`, `auto_rebalance.py` rewire, unclassified-bucket link, AC wording on new-cash totals, `PUT /rebalance/{owner}/policy` tolerance validation, partial-update semantics).

## LLM tier

Haiku — this is a mechanical, single-file test addition mirroring an existing assertion pattern.

## Success looks like

- `tests/test_app.py` contains a test that issues `POST` to the removed rebalance path and asserts `405`.
- The full test suite passes locally and in CI.
- The existing `DELETE` → 405 assertion still passes unchanged.

## Failure looks like

- The new test asserts 404, 200, or 422 instead of 405 (indicates the route is being matched by something unexpected, or the assertion is wrong).
- Production code in `backend/routes/rebalance.py` is modified.
- The existing `DELETE` → 405 test is deleted or weakened to make the new test pass.
- The test is added but skipped, xfailed, or gated behind a marker.

_Follow-up from AI review of PR #9466._

items.title: Report 8 (Feature Request): Desktop Icons and Managing Files Directly on the Desktop Is your feature request related to a problem?
items.body:
Please describe.

I'm frustrated that files located in the ~/Desktop folder do not appear on the actual desktop screen, and files cannot be dragged and dropped directly onto the desktop wallpaper area for quick staging and access.

Describe the solution you'd like

Add support for desktop icons in COSMIC, allowing users to:

View, organize, rename, and launch files/folders stored in ~/Desktop directly on the desktop background.

Drag and drop files from COSMIC Files or web browsers directly onto the desktop wallpaper.

Have an option in Settings to toggle desktop icons on or off.

Describe alternatives you've considered

Opening a dedicated COSMIC Files window navigated to ~/Desktop.

Third-party desktop icon extensions (which are not natively compatible with the Rust-based COSMIC desktop).

Additional context

Many users rely on the desktop surface as a temporary workspace for documents and active downloads.

items.title: Report 1 (Bug): Web Apps (PWAs) Do Not Display Proper Application Icons
items.body:
When installing or creating a shortcut for a web app / Progressive Web App (PWA) from a web browser (e.g., Chrome, Chromium, Brave), the application shortcut created in the COSMIC App Library does not display its proper site icon/favicon. Instead, it shows a generic placeholder or system fallback icon.

To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

Open a browser (e.g., Chrome, Brave, Chromium).

Navigate to any website supporting web app installation (e.g., Spotify, YouTube, X/Twitter).

Click "Install [App]" or go to browser settings and select "Create shortcut... / Install page as app".

Open the COSMIC App Library / Application Launcher.

Search for or locate the newly installed web app.

Observe that the launcher icon is a generic/fallback icon instead of the web app's official icon.

Expected behavior

The desktop entry should properly read the cached/installed icon path specified in the .desktop file and render the correct high-resolution application icon in the app launcher and dock.

Screenshots

(N/A)

Desktop (please complete the following information):

OS: Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS (COSMIC Desktop)

Additional context

The .desktop files generated in ~/.local/share/applications/ contain the Icon= parameter pointing to browser-cached icons, but COSMIC's app library does not seem to resolve or display them properly.

items.title: [PHASE1-E] Interop Route Registry + Python↔C bridge
items.body:
## Source / authority

- Short-term roadmap: #9 S4
- Technical specification: #4 §§2.5, 9–10, 14.5, 17.5, 19, 20-D, 26.1–26.2, 26.5
- Accepted base: main `e7c790fda35209b6be5bc9f910d76a7db6f6fff6`
- Python importer: #7 / PR #8
- C importer: #12 / PR #13
- Shared renderer: #10 / PR #11
- Repository Control: kinoko34077/devflow#350

## Objective

Implement the smallest deterministic interoperability Route Registry/Resolver and represent the first Python→C route through existing `ctypes → C ABI` machinery.

This stage proves **route resolution and inspectability**, not runtime execution. S5 owns Execution Plan/runtime execution.

## Architecture

Keep route/planner data outside the mandatory Graph Core schema.

A route registration describes:
- source contract/domain;
- target contract/domain;
- graph-visible bridge Block/reference;
- whether the route is executable in the current environment;
- explicit runtime requirements;
- minimal transfer semantics where applicable.

The selected route MUST be convertible to an inspectable ordinary Algoram Graph:
- collapsed view MAY show endpoint→endpoint;
- expanded route MUST expose the actual registered bridge path;
- route reachability MUST NOT imply semantic equivalence/substitutability.

## Required resolver behavior

Priority:
1. explicit requested route, when valid;
2. valid direct route;
3. otherwise valid route with the fewest connector hops;
4. deterministic tie-break.

Search MUST be bounded and cycle-safe.

The resolver MUST distinguish:
- direct route found;
- indirect route found;
- no direct route but indirect route exists;
- no known route.

## First registered route

Represent:

```text
Python
→ ctypes
→ C ABI
→ C
```

using an existing-mechanism bridge definition. No Algoram-specific FFI implementation is created.

The route MAY be represented as one registered high-level bridge with an inspectable internal Graph containing the ctypes/C-ABI steps.

## Transfer semantics

Only route-local metadata, where applicable:
- copy | borrow | move | proxy
- sync | async

Do not create a universal Algoram value/ownership/effect taxonomy.

## Acceptance

- [ ] separate bounded interop crate/module builds against accepted `algoram-core`.
- [ ] registry can register routes without modifying core Graph schema.
- [ ] explicit valid route wins.
- [ ] otherwise direct valid route wins.
- [ ] otherwise fewest-hop valid route wins.
- [ ] deterministic tie-break is tested.
- [ ] cyclic route data terminates safely.
- [ ] bounded search can return unresolved rather than exploring indefinitely.
- [ ] environment/runtime requirements can invalidate an otherwise matching route.
- [ ] `no direct route` is distinguishable from `no known route`.
- [ ] reachability does not mark endpoints equivalent/substitutable.
- [ ] selected route exposes transfer + sync/async semantics.
- [ ] Python→ctypes→C ABI→C route is represented and expandable as ordinary Graph/Blocks.
- [ ] existing core/Python/C/UI verification remains GREEN.

## Excludes

- actually executing ctypes/C code;
- Execution Plan/runtime dispatch;
- benchmark-based route choice;
- cost/energy/quality ranking;
- universal type system;
- semantic equivalence inference;
- automatic substitutability inference;
- marketplace/cloud/failover.

## Next Action

`[IMPLEMENT] Add a bounded interop registry/resolver crate and Python→ctypes→C ABI→C inspectable fixture. Verify resolver precedence, bounded/cycle-safe search, environment constraints and full regression CI.`
